sec.salah.title: Salah, Sunnah & Dhikr
sec.salah.note: Whoever attends Isha in congregation has the reward of standing half the night. And whoever prays Isha and Fajr in congregation has the reward of standing the entire night.
sec.quran.title: Quran — Understand & Implement
sec.quran.note: Recite the Quran, for on the Day of Resurrection it will come as an intercessor for its companions.
sec.character.title: Intention, Heart & Character
sec.character.note: Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will get what they intended.
sec.charity.title: Charity & Service
sec.charity.note: The Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was most generous in Ramadan.
sec.lastTen.title: Last Ten Nights — Seek Laylatul Qadr
sec.lastTen.note: "Seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days." — Bukhari 2017. It could be ANY of the last ten nights — strive every single night.
sec.avoidance.title: Daily Avoidance Check
sec.avoidance.note: Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of him giving up his food and drink.
sec.abuBakr.title: Abu Bakr Challenge
sec.abuBakr.note: The Prophet ﷺ asked four questions. Abu Bakr answered "I did" to all. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever combines these will enter Jannah."
deed.fajr-sunnah.label: 2 Sunnah before Fajr
deed.fajr-sunnah.exp: Better than the world and all it contains.
deed.fajr.label: Fajr prayer
deed.fajr.exp: Foundation of the day; the angels of night and day witness it.
deed.morning-adhkar.label: Morning adhkar
deed.morning-adhkar.exp: Saying Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru... 3 times in the morning: no sudden affliction strikes until evening.
deed.istighfar.label: Istighfar (seek forgiveness)
deed.istighfar.exp: The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness more than 70 times daily.
deed.salawat.label: Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ
deed.salawat.exp: One salawat brings ten blessings from Allah.
deed.duha.label: Duha prayer (2 or more rakahs)
deed.duha.exp: Two rakahs of Duha suffice for the charity due on every joint each morning.
deed.dhuhr-sunnah-before.label: 4 Sunnah before Dhuhr
deed.dhuhr-sunnah-before.exp: The Prophet ﷺ never missed four rakahs before Dhuhr.
deed.dhuhr.label: Dhuhr prayer
deed.dhuhr.exp: Midday obligation — establishes rhythm of worship.
deed.dhuhr-sunnah-after.label: 2 Sunnah after Dhuhr
deed.dhuhr-sunnah-after.exp: Twelve daily Sunnah rakahs earn a house in Jannah.
deed.asr.label: Asr prayer
deed.dua-iftar.label: Dua at iftar
deed.dua-iftar.exp: At iftar the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Thirst has gone, the veins are moist, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills."
deed.maghrib.label: Maghrib prayer
deed.maghrib.exp: The Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib when the sun had set.
deed.maghrib-sunnah.label: 2 Sunnah after Maghrib
deed.maghrib-sunnah.exp: Prayed regularly by the Prophet ﷺ.
deed.evening-adhkar.label: Evening adhkar
deed.evening-adhkar.exp: Saying Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru... 3 times in the evening: no sudden affliction strikes until morning.
deed.isha.label: Isha prayer
deed.isha.exp: Praying Isha and Fajr in congregation is like standing the whole night in prayer.
deed.isha-sunnah.label: 2 Sunnah after Isha
deed.isha-sunnah.exp: Two after Isha are among the twelve daily rakahs for which a house is built in Paradise.
deed.tarawih.label: Tarawih
deed.tarawih.exp: Whoever prays the nights of Ramadan with faith and hoping for reward has his past sins forgiven.
deed.witr.label: Witr prayer
deed.witr.exp: Make it your last prayer of the night.
deed.night-adhkar.label: Night adhkar before sleep
deed.night-adhkar.exp: Recite Ayat al-Kursi when you go to bed: a guard from Allah stays with you and no devil comes near you till morning.
deed.tahajjud.label: Tahajjud (last third of night)
deed.tahajjud.exp: Allah descends and asks: "Who calls upon Me that I may answer?"
deed.dua-night.label: Dua in last third of night
deed.dua-night.exp: In the last third of every night Allah offers to answer whoever calls, give whoever asks and forgive whoever seeks it.
deed.istighfar-sleep.label: Istighfar before sleep
deed.istighfar-sleep.exp: Whoever says Sayyid al-Istighfar at night with firm faith and dies before morning is of the people of Paradise.
deed.accountability.label: Self-accountability (muhasaba)
deed.accountability.exp: "Let every soul look to what it has sent forth for tomorrow."
deed.renew-tomorrow.label: Renewed intention for tomorrow
deed.renew-tomorrow.exp: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent.
deed.sleep-early.label: Slept early for Fajr
deed.sleep-early.exp: The Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before Isha and talking after it. Protect your Fajr.
deed.quran-recitation.label: Quran recitation (daily portion)
deed.quran-recitation.exp: Ramadan is the month of Quran — recite your daily pages.
deed.quran-reflection.label: Reflected on meaning (tadabbur)
deed.quran-reflection.exp: Pondering deeply transforms the heart and guides action.
deed.quran-implementation.label: Applied a lesson from today's reading
deed.quran-listening.label: Listened to Quran recitation
deed.quran-listening.exp: Listen and be silent so that you may receive mercy.
deed.quran-memorization.label: Memorised new ayah(s)
deed.quran-memorization.exp: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
deed.intention.label: Renewed intention (ikhlas)
deed.intention.exp: Every action takes its value from the heart.
deed.riya.label: Checked and corrected riya
deed.tongue.label: Guarded the tongue
deed.tongue.exp: Fasting disciplines speech as much as hunger.
deed.arguments.label: Avoided arguments while fasting
deed.gaze.label: Lowered the gaze
deed.gaze.exp: What the eyes consume shapes the heart.
deed.anger.label: Controlled anger
deed.anger.exp: The strong one controls himself when angry.
deed.gentleness.label: Chose gentleness in interactions
deed.gentleness.exp: Nothing is heavier on the Scale than good character.
deed.mercy.label: Showed mercy to others
deed.mercy.exp: The Merciful shows mercy to those who show mercy.
deed.humility.label: Practised humility
deed.humility.exp: Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah will raise him.
deed.forgave.label: Forgave someone
deed.forgave.exp: Whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is with Allah.
deed.dua-absence.label: Made dua for someone in their absence
deed.dua-absence.exp: An angel says: "Amin, and for you the same."
deed.made-happy.label: Made someone happy for Allah's sake
deed.made-happy.exp: Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
deed.charity-given.label: Gave charity (any amount)
deed.fed-fasting.label: Fed someone who was fasting
deed.fed-fasting.exp: You receive the same reward as the fasting person.
deed.helped-family.label: Served or helped parents/family
deed.helped-family.exp: After prayer on time, the deed most loved by Allah is kindness to parents.
deed.maintained-ties.label: Maintained ties of kinship
deed.maintained-ties.exp: Whoever maintains family ties, Allah maintains ties with him.
deed.visited-sick.label: Visited or supported the sick
deed.visited-sick.exp: Whoever visits a sick person remains in the harvest of Paradise until he returns.
deed.dua-others.label: Made dua for others privately
deed.dua-others.exp: An angel says: "Amin, and for you the same."
deed.laylat-qadr.label: Sought Laylat al-Qadr tonight
deed.laylat-qadr.exp: Better than 1,000 months. Strive every night.
deed.extra-dua.label: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul 'afwa fa'fu 'anni
deed.extra-dua.exp: The dua the Prophet ﷺ taught Aishah for Laylatul Qadr.
deed.extra-quran.label: Extra Quran recitation
deed.extra-quran.exp: Every night of Ramadan until it ended, the Prophet ﷺ recited the Quran to Jibril.
deed.night-charity.label: Night charity (hidden sadaqah)
deed.night-charity.exp: Hidden charity — his left hand does not know what his right gives.
deed.long-sujood.label: Extra long sujood with dua
deed.long-sujood.exp: The closest a servant is to Allah is in sujood.
deed.dua-list.label: Personal dua list — recited with conviction
deed.dua-list.exp: Prepare your requests for these blessed nights.
deed.itikaf.label: I'tikaf (even partial)
deed.itikaf.exp: The Prophet ﷺ used to observe I'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan.
deed.no-lying.label: No lying
deed.no-lying.exp: Allah has no need of someone giving up food and drink if they do not give up false speech and acting on it.
deed.no-backbiting.label: No backbiting (gheebah)
deed.no-backbiting.exp: Like eating the flesh of your dead brother.
deed.no-riya.label: No showing off (riya)
deed.no-riya.exp: Deeds done for show are rejected.
deed.no-excess-media.label: No excessive social media
deed.no-excess-media.exp: The believers turn away from ill speech.
deed.no-useless-scrolling.label: No useless scrolling
deed.no-useless-scrolling.exp: Many people lose out on two blessings: health and free time.
deed.no-haram-content.label: No haram or inappropriate content
deed.no-haram-content.exp: The hearing, sight and heart will all be questioned.
deed.no-overeating.label: No overeating at iftar
deed.no-overeating.exp: A few bites are enough; if you must eat more, a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath.
deed.no-wasting-food.label: No wasting food
deed.no-wasting-food.exp: Allah does not love the wasteful.
deed.no-neglect-salah.label: No neglecting prayers
deed.no-neglect-salah.exp: There came successors who neglected prayer and pursued desires.
deed.abu-bakr-fasting.label: "Who among you is fasting today?" — I am.
deed.abu-bakr-funeral.label: "Who attended a funeral?" — I did.
deed.abu-bakr-funeral.exp: Following a funeral and joining its janazah prayer.
deed.abu-bakr-fed.label: "Who fed a poor person?" — I did.
deed.abu-bakr-fed.exp: Even a small meal or date counts.
deed.abu-bakr-sick.label: "Who visited a sick person?" — I did.
hadith.1: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
hadith.2: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of Hell are closed.
hadith.3: Fasting is a shield; so when one of you is fasting, let him not speak obscenely or act ignorantly.
hadith.4: There is a gate in Paradise called Ar-Rayyan, through which only those who fast will enter.
hadith.5: Whoever gives iftar to a fasting person will have the same reward without reducing theirs.
hadith.6: When My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.
hadith.7: Recite the Quran, for on the Day of Resurrection it will come as an intercessor for its companions.
hadith.8: Allah said: Every action of the son of Adam is for him except fasting, for it is for Me and I shall reward it.
hadith.9: Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of his giving up his food and drink.
hadith.10: Seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan.
hadith.11: Whoever gives charity equal to a date from good earnings, Allah accepts it and grows it until it becomes like a mountain.
hadith.12: Whoever stands in prayer on Laylatul Qadr out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins will be forgiven.
hadith.13: The Prophet ﷺ was the most generous in Ramadan when Jibreel would meet him.
hadith.14: Fasting the month of patience (Ramadan) and three days of every month is fasting for a lifetime.
hadith.15: When the last ten days began, the Prophet ﷺ would tighten his waist belt, stay up the night in worship and wake his family.
hadith.16: Take to fasting, for there is nothing like it.
hadith.17: The breath of a fasting person is sweeter to Allah than the scent of musk.
hadith.18: Whoever prays qiyam in Ramadan with faith and seeking reward, his past sins will be forgiven.
hadith.19: When you make dua, do not say 'if You wish'; ask with firm resolve, for nothing is too great for Allah to give.
hadith.20: The strong is not the one who overcomes people, but who controls himself when angry.
hadith.21: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.
hadith.22: By his good character, a believer attains the rank of one who fasts by day and prays at night.
hadith.23: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul 'afwa fa'fu 'anni — O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
hadith.24: The one who recites Quran skillfully is with the noble scribes (angels).
hadith.25: Allah extends His hand at night to accept repentance of those who sinned by day.
hadith.26: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
hadith.27: Nothing is heavier on the Scale than good character.
hadith.28: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
hadith.30: Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted forever.

tf.tf001.q: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward will have their previous sins forgiven.
tf.tf001.x: The Prophet ﷺ promised forgiveness of past sins for fasting Ramadan with faith and hope of reward.
tf.tf002.q: The special gate of Paradise reserved for those who fast is called Al-Firdaus.
tf.tf002.x: The gate is called Ar-Rayyan — only those who fast will enter through it.
tf.tf003.q: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of Hell are closed.
tf.tf003.x: In the same hadith the Prophet ﷺ said the devils are chained, so make the most of this month.
tf.tf004.q: Whoever gives iftar to a fasting person receives half of that person's reward.
tf.tf004.x: They receive the SAME reward — without reducing the fasting person's reward at all.
tf.tf005.q: The Prophet ﷺ described fasting as a shield.
tf.tf005.x: Fasting shields you — so the fasting person should not speak obscenely or act ignorantly.
tf.tf006.q: The dua of a fasting person can be rejected like anyone else's.
tf.tf006.x: The Prophet ﷺ said three supplications are not turned back: a parent's, a fasting person's and a traveller's. So make plenty of dua while fasting.
tf.tf007.q: Allah says every deed of the son of Adam is for himself, except fasting — which is for Allah, and He Himself will reward it.
tf.tf007.x: Allah singles out fasting as His own and says He Himself will reward it. The same hadith says the fasting person has two joys: at iftar and when he meets his Lord.
tf.tf008.q: If you keep up false speech while fasting, Allah has no need of you giving up your food and drink.
tf.tf008.x: Fasting is more than leaving food and drink: the fasting person should also give up false speech and acting on it.
tf.tf009.q: If someone insults you while fasting, the Sunnah is to respond with a sharper insult.
tf.tf009.x: The Prophet ﷺ said that if someone fights or insults a fasting person, he should say twice: 'I am fasting.'
tf.tf010.q: The breath of a fasting person is sweeter to Allah than the scent of musk.
tf.tf010.x: The changed smell of a fasting person's mouth may seem unpleasant to people, yet the Prophet ﷺ said it is better in Allah's sight than musk.
tf.tf011.q: Fasting Ramadan and then six days of Shawwal is like fasting the whole year.
tf.tf011.x: The Prophet ﷺ said that fasting six days after Eid al-Fitr completes the year, because whoever does a good deed gets the reward of ten like it.
tf.tf012.q: The Prophet ﷺ said a few bites to keep one's back straight are enough, and if one must eat more: a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath.
tf.tf012.x: The Prophet ﷺ warned against overfilling the stomach — a lesson especially relevant at iftar.
tf.tf013.q: Praying Isha and Fajr in congregation carries the reward of standing the entire night in prayer.
tf.tf013.x: Isha in congregation = half the night; adding Fajr in congregation = the whole night.
tf.tf014.q: The two Sunnah rakahs before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.
tf.tf014.x: Two short rakahs outweigh the entire dunya — never skip them.
tf.tf015.q: Whoever prays qiyam (night prayer) in Ramadan with faith and seeking reward will be forgiven their past sins.
tf.tf015.x: This is the promise behind Tarawih and night prayer in Ramadan.
tf.tf016.q: The Prophet ﷺ told us to make witr the last prayer of the night.
tf.tf016.x: He ﷺ said: Make witr your last prayer at night. Let it close your night of worship.
tf.tf017.q: The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness (istighfar) more than 70 times every day.
tf.tf017.x: If the forgiven Prophet ﷺ did istighfar daily, how much more do we need it?
tf.tf018.q: Sending one salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ brings ten blessings from Allah.
tf.tf018.x: Every single salawat is multiplied ten times over.
tf.tf019.q: Allah descends in the FIRST third of the night asking: 'Who calls upon Me that I may answer?'
tf.tf019.x: It is the LAST third of the night — the most blessed time for dua and tahajjud.
tf.tf020.q: Duha prayer counts as charity for every joint in your body.
tf.tf020.x: Each morning charity is due on every joint of your body, and two rakahs of Duha suffice for it all.
tf.tf021.q: Praying twelve Sunnah rakahs daily earns you a house in Jannah.
tf.tf021.x: Pray twelve voluntary rakahs each day besides the obligatory prayers, and Allah will build you a house in Paradise.
tf.tf022.q: Reciting Ayatul Kursi when going to bed brings a guard from Allah through the night.
tf.tf022.x: The Prophet ﷺ confirmed it: a guard from Allah stays with you, and Satan will not come near you until morning.
tf.tf023.q: The Prophet ﷺ enjoyed long conversations after Isha.
tf.tf023.x: He disliked talking after Isha — sleep early and protect your Fajr.
tf.tf024.q: The most beloved deeds to Allah are grand one-time gestures rather than small consistent ones.
tf.tf024.x: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most CONSISTENT, even if small.
tf.tf025.q: The Quran was revealed in the month of Ramadan as guidance for mankind.
tf.tf025.x: That is why Ramadan is called the month of the Quran.
tf.tf026.q: On the Day of Resurrection, the Quran will come as an intercessor for those who recite it.
tf.tf026.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: Recite the Quran, for it will come as an intercessor for its companions. Be one of its companions this Ramadan.
tf.tf027.q: The one who recites the Quran skillfully will be with the noble scribes (angels).
tf.tf027.x: And the one who struggles while reciting receives DOUBLE reward — so keep reading either way.
tf.tf028.q: The widely used Madinah mushaf of the Quran has 604 pages.
tf.tf028.x: That's why this app tracks 604 pages — about 20 pages a day completes it in 30 days.
tf.tf029.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.'
tf.tf029.x: Memorising even one new ayah puts you on this path.
tf.tf030.q: When the Quran is recited, we are commanded to listen attentively and be silent so we may receive mercy.
tf.tf030.x: Even listening to recitation is a rewarded act of worship.
tf.tf031.q: Tadabbur means reciting the Quran as fast as possible.
tf.tf031.x: Tadabbur is deep REFLECTION on the meaning — pondering transforms the heart and guides action.
tf.tf032.q: Jibreel would review the Quran with the Prophet ﷺ every Ramadan.
tf.tf032.x: Jibreel met him every night of Ramadan to study the Quran together — revise your Quran in Ramadan.
tf.tf033.q: The Quran is divided into 40 juz.
tf.tf033.x: The Quran has 30 juz — reading about one juz a day completes it in Ramadan.
tf.tf034.q: The Quran criticises those who command others to righteousness while forgetting themselves.
tf.tf034.x: Knowledge without action is incomplete — apply a lesson from today's reading.
tf.tf035.q: Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will get what they intended.
tf.tf035.x: The very first hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari — every deed takes its value from the heart.
tf.tf036.q: The strong person is the one who defeats others in wrestling.
tf.tf036.x: The strong is the one who CONTROLS HIMSELF when angry.
tf.tf037.q: Nothing is heavier on the Scale on the Day of Judgment than good character.
tf.tf037.x: The Prophet ﷺ said this of the believer's Scale, and added that Allah hates the obscene, foul-mouthed person.
tf.tf038.q: The Quran compares backbiting to eating the flesh of your dead brother.
tf.tf038.x: Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it.
tf.tf039.q: Riya (showing off) only slightly reduces a deed's reward — the deed still counts.
tf.tf039.x: Deeds done for show are REJECTED entirely. Riya quietly voids reward.
tf.tf040.q: When you make dua for your brother or sister in Islam in their absence, an angel says: 'Amin, and for you the same.'
tf.tf040.x: The Prophet ﷺ said such a dua is answered, and the angel appointed to the one praying says this whenever he asks good for his brother.
tf.tf041.q: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
tf.tf041.x: In the same hadith the Prophet ﷺ told believers not to harm their neighbours and to honour their guests.
tf.tf042.q: Humbling yourself for Allah's sake lowers your status among people.
tf.tf042.x: Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah will RAISE him.
tf.tf043.q: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
tf.tf043.x: Character starts at home — with the people who see you every day.
tf.tf044.q: Through good character, a believer can reach the rank of one who fasts by day and prays at night.
tf.tf044.x: The Prophet ﷺ said a believer, by his good character, attains the rank of the one who fasts and stands in prayer.
tf.tf045.q: Allah extends His hand at night to accept the repentance of those who sinned during the day.
tf.tf045.x: And by day for those who sinned at night, until the sun rises from the west.
tf.tf046.q: The Prophet ﷺ was at his most generous during Ramadan.
tf.tf046.x: He was the most generous of people — and even more so in Ramadan when Jibreel met him.
tf.tf047.x: Charity does NOT decrease wealth, and Allah says whatever you spend, He will replace it (Quran 34:39).
tf.tf048.q: The Prophet ﷺ said charity extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire.
tf.tf048.x: He listed it among the doors of good, along with fasting, which is a shield, and prayer in the depth of the night.
tf.tf049.q: Whoever visits a sick person remains in the 'harvest of Paradise' until he returns.
tf.tf049.x: Asked what the harvest of Paradise is, the Prophet ﷺ said: its gathered fruit.
tf.tf050.q: In the famous hadith of the four questions, it was Umar (RA) who answered 'I did' to all four.
tf.tf050.x: It was ABU BAKR (RA) — fasting, following a funeral, feeding the poor, and visiting the sick, all in one day.
tf.tf051.q: Whoever combines fasting, attending a funeral, feeding the poor, and visiting the sick in a single day will enter Jannah.
tf.tf051.x: This is the Abu Bakr Challenge in your Today tab — try to complete all four in one day!
tf.tf052.q: Whoever maintains family ties, Allah maintains ties with him.
tf.tf052.x: The Prophet ﷺ said the tie of kinship hangs from the Throne and says: whoever joins me, Allah joins him, and whoever cuts me off, Allah cuts him off.
tf.tf053.q: Islam teaches that charity is best given publicly so others can see it.
tf.tf053.x: Hidden charity is praised — giving so secretly that the left hand does not know what the right hand gives.
tf.tf054.q: Giving food in charity only counts if it is a full meal.
tf.tf054.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: Save yourselves from the Fire, even by giving half a date in charity.
tf.tf055.q: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.
tf.tf055.x: One night of worship outweighs over 83 years — a lifetime of deeds.
tf.tf056.q: Laylatul Qadr is guaranteed to fall on the 27th night every year.
tf.tf056.x: We are told to seek it in the ODD nights of the last ten — it could be any of them, so strive every night.
tf.tf057.q: We are instructed to seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days.
tf.tf057.x: Nights 21, 23, 25, 27, and 29 — this app highlights them for you.
tf.tf058.q: When the last ten days began, the Prophet ﷺ would tighten his waist belt and stay up the night in worship.
tf.tf058.x: He exerted himself in these nights more than at any other time — and woke his family too.
tf.tf059.q: The dua the Prophet ﷺ taught Aishah (RA) for Laylatul Qadr is: 'Allahumma innaka afuwwun tuhibbul afwa fafu anni.'
tf.tf059.x: 'O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love pardon, so pardon me.' Aishah had asked what to say if she knew which night was Laylatul Qadr.
tf.tf060.q: The Prophet ﷺ observed I'tikaf only once in his life.
tf.tf060.x: Aishah reported that he ﷺ used to observe i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan until he passed away, and his wives did so after him.
tf.tf061.q: Standing in prayer on Laylatul Qadr with faith and hope of reward forgives past sins.
tf.tf061.x: Pray in the last ten nights with faith and hope of Allah's reward, so you do not miss this forgiveness of previous sins.
tf.tf062.q: The closest a servant is to Allah is while in sujood.
tf.tf062.x: Lengthen your sujood in the last ten nights and pour out your duas there.
tf.tf063.q: Allah frees people from the Fire only in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
tf.tf063.x: The Prophet ﷺ said that at every iftar Allah has people He frees from the Fire, and that happens every night. The popular Mercy, Forgiveness and Salvation thirds come from a weak narration.
tf.tf-fast-01.q: The Prophet ﷺ said a fasting person has two moments of joy: one when breaking the fast, and one when meeting their Lord.
tf.tf-fast-01.x: In Bukhari and Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ said the one who fasts has two joys: joy when breaking the fast, and joy when meeting his Lord, pleased because of his fasting.
tf.tf-fast-02.q: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever fasts one day in the way of Allah, Allah will distance their face from the Fire by seventy years.
tf.tf-fast-02.x: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported this from the Prophet ﷺ in Bukhari and Muslim: a single day of fasting in the way of Allah keeps a person's face seventy years away from the Fire.
tf.tf-fast-03.q: The Prophet ﷺ discouraged eating suhoor, teaching that a fast without it earns more reward.
tf.tf-fast-03.x: He ﷺ encouraged it, saying: 'Take suhoor, for in suhoor there is blessing.' (Bukhari and Muslim). The pre-dawn meal is a blessed Sunnah.
tf.tf-fast-04.q: When Zayd ibn Thabit ate suhoor with the Prophet ﷺ, they finished it hours before the adhan for Fajr.
tf.tf-fast-04.x: Zayd ibn Thabit said the gap between their suhoor with the Prophet ﷺ and the adhan was only about the time it takes to recite fifty verses (Sahih al-Bukhari). They ate suhoor close to dawn.
tf.tf-fast-05.q: The Sunnah is to wait a while after sunset before breaking the fast, rather than breaking it straight away.
tf.tf-fast-05.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'People will remain upon good as long as they hasten to break the fast.' (Bukhari and Muslim). Breaking the fast promptly once the sun has set is the Sunnah.
tf.tf-fast-06.q: The Prophet ﷺ would pray Maghrib first and only break his fast after the prayer.
tf.tf-fast-06.x: Anas said the Prophet ﷺ broke his fast before praying, with fresh dates; if there were none, dried dates; and if none, a few sips of water (Abu Dawud, graded hasan sahih by al-Albani).
tf.tf-fast-07.q: When breaking his fast, the Prophet ﷺ would say: 'Thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.'
tf.tf-fast-07.x: Ibn Umar reported that at iftar the Prophet ﷺ would say: Dhahabaz-zama'u wabtallatil-'uruqu wa thabatal-ajru in sha Allah. Recorded by Abu Dawud and graded hasan by al-Albani.
tf.tf-fast-08.q: The Prophet ﷺ said that if a fasting person eats or drinks forgetfully, they should stop fasting for the rest of that day.
tf.tf-fast-08.x: He ﷺ said: 'If someone forgets and eats or drinks, let him complete his fast, for it is Allah who fed him and gave him drink.' (Bukhari and Muslim).
tf.tf-fast-09.q: The Prophet ﷺ warned that some people fast yet gain nothing from their fasting except hunger.
tf.tf-fast-09.x: He ﷺ said some who fast get nothing but hunger, and some who pray at night get nothing but sleeplessness (Ibn Majah). He also said Allah has no need of the fast of one who does not give up lying and acting on it (Bukhari 1903).
tf.tf-fast-10.q: The Quran allows a person who is ill or on a journey during Ramadan to fast an equal number of other days instead.
tf.tf-fast-10.x: Allah says: 'Whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days.' (Quran 2:184). The same allowance is repeated in the next verse, 2:185.
tf.tf-fast-11.q: In the verses on fasting Ramadan, Allah says He wants hardship for the believers rather than ease.
tf.tf-fast-11.x: Allah says the opposite in Quran 2:185, right after excusing the ill and the traveller: 'Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship.'
tf.tf-fast-12.q: Fasting six days of Shawwal is obligatory, just like fasting the month of Ramadan.
tf.tf-fast-12.x: When a Bedouin asked what fasting Allah made compulsory, the Prophet ﷺ named the month of Ramadan and said anything more is voluntary (Bukhari and Muslim). So the six days of Shawwal are a voluntary fast.
tf.tf-fast-13.q: The Prophet ﷺ said he hoped that fasting the Day of Arafah would expiate the sins of the year before it and the year after it.
tf.tf-fast-13.x: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ said this about fasting the Day of Arafah, and said that fasting the day of Ashura expiates the sins of the year before it.
tf.tf-fast-14.q: When the Prophet ﷺ learned that Ashura was the day Allah saved Musa (Moses) from Pharaoh, he fasted it and told the Muslims to fast it.
tf.tf-fast-14.x: Ibn Abbas said the Jews of Madinah fasted Ashura for this reason. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'I am closer to Musa than they,' then fasted it and ordered it to be fasted. It became optional once Ramadan was made obligatory (Bukhari 2002).
tf.tf-fast-15.q: Some Companions had their young children fast on Ashura and gave them wool toys to distract them from hunger until iftar.
tf.tf-fast-15.x: Ar-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh said they made their children fast on Ashura, and when a child cried for food they gave him a wool toy until it was time to break the fast (Bukhari and Muslim).
tf.tf-salah-01.q: The Prophet ﷺ stopped leading the night prayer in the mosque in Ramadan because too few people came.
tf.tf-salah-01.x: The mosque grew so full it could not hold them. He ﷺ said their presence was not hidden from him, but he feared the night prayer would be made obligatory on them and they would be unable to do it (Bukhari 2012).
tf.tf-salah-02.q: Whoever prays the night prayer with the imam until he finishes is recorded as having prayed the whole night.
tf.tf-salah-02.x: The Prophet ﷺ said this in Ramadan, when the Companions asked him to lead them for the rest of the night (Tirmidhi 806, graded Sahih). So stay with the imam until he finishes.
tf.tf-salah-03.q: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is Witr (One) and loves witr, meaning odd numbers.
tf.tf-salah-03.x: Witr means single or odd-numbered. In Bukhari 6410 the Prophet ﷺ said Allah is Witr and loves witr, and he told us to make the witr prayer the last of our prayer at night (Bukhari 998).
tf.tf-salah-04.q: The Prophet ﷺ only ever prayed witr in the last part of the night.
tf.tf-salah-04.x: Aishah said he prayed witr in the early, middle and last parts of the night (Muslim 745). He advised anyone who fears not waking up to pray witr before sleeping (Muslim 755).
tf.tf-salah-05.q: The Prophet ﷺ said the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer at night.
tf.tf-salah-05.x: In Muslim 1163 he ﷺ said the most excellent prayer after the obligatory ones is prayer at night, and the most excellent fast after Ramadan is in Allah's month, Muharram.
tf.tf-salah-06.q: The Prophet ﷺ said the prayer most beloved to Allah is that of Prophet Dawud, who slept half the night and prayed a third of it.
tf.tf-salah-06.x: In Bukhari 1131 he ﷺ said Dawud slept half the night, prayed for a third of it, then slept for a sixth. His fast, every other day, is also the fast most beloved to Allah.
tf.tf-salah-07.q: When Ibn Mas'ud asked which deed Allah loves most, the Prophet ﷺ first named kindness to parents.
tf.tf-salah-07.x: He ﷺ first named prayer offered at its proper time, then kindness to parents, then jihad in Allah's cause (Bukhari 527).
tf.tf-salah-08.q: The Prophet ﷺ said prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than praying alone.
tf.tf-salah-08.x: Ibn Umar narrated this in Bukhari 645. Abu Hurairah's narration says twenty-five times (Bukhari 647). Both are authentic reports of the great reward of praying together.
tf.tf-salah-09.q: Sitting in the mosque waiting for the prayer to begin earns no reward.
tf.tf-salah-09.x: The Prophet ﷺ said a person counts as being in prayer while he waits for it, and the angels ask Allah to forgive him and have mercy on him while he stays in his place of prayer and keeps his wudu (Bukhari 659).
tf.tf-salah-10.q: In the hadith promising a house in Paradise for twelve voluntary rak'ahs a day, all twelve are prayed after the obligatory prayers.
tf.tf-salah-10.x: Some come before. The Prophet ﷺ listed four rak'ahs before Dhuhr, two after it, two after Maghrib, two after Isha and two before Fajr (Tirmidhi 415).
tf.tf-salah-11.q: Surah al-Mu'minun begins by describing successful believers as those who are humbly focused (khushu) in their prayer.
tf.tf-salah-11.x: It opens: Certainly will the believers have succeeded: they who are during their prayer humbly intent (Quran 23:1-2).
tf.tf-salah-12.q: The Prophet ﷺ described looking around during prayer as something Satan snatches from a person's prayer.
tf.tf-salah-12.x: When Aishah asked about glancing around in prayer, he ﷺ said it is a snatching by which Satan steals from the servant's prayer (Bukhari 751). Keep your focus on your prayer.
tf.tf-salah-13.q: The first deed a servant will be held to account for on the Day of Judgment is fasting.
tf.tf-salah-13.x: It is prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said the first thing a servant is held to account for is the prayer, and the first matter judged between people is bloodshed (Nasa'i 3991).
tf.tf-salah-14.q: The Prophet ﷺ heard Bilal's footsteps in Paradise, and Bilal said his most hopeful deed was praying after every wudu.
tf.tf-salah-14.x: Bilal said that whenever he made wudu, by night or day, he prayed with it whatever was written for him to pray (Bukhari 1149).
tf.tf-salah-15.q: Wudu cleans the body, but it does not wipe away any sins.
tf.tf-salah-15.x: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever performs wudu well, his sins leave his body, even from under his nails (Muslim 245).
tf.tf-quran-01.q: In Surah Ad-Dukhan, Allah describes the night in which He sent down the Quran as 'a blessed night'.
tf.tf-quran-01.x: Allah says: 'Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night' (Quran 44:3). In Surah Al-Qadr He says He sent it down during the Night of Decree (97:1).
tf.tf-quran-02.q: The month of Ramadan is mentioned by name many times in the Quran.
tf.tf-quran-02.x: Ramadan is named only once in the whole Quran: in Quran 2:185, which says the Quran was revealed in that month as guidance for the people.
tf.tf-quran-03.q: The Quran was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ all at once, in a single night.
tf.tf-quran-03.x: Allah sent the Quran down on a blessed night (Quran 44:3), but it reached the Prophet ﷺ in stages (17:106). When disbelievers asked why it was not revealed all at once, Allah said this was to strengthen his heart (25:32).
tf.tf-quran-04.q: In the cave of Hira, when the angel first said 'Read!', the Prophet ﷺ replied that he did not know how to read.
tf.tf-quran-04.x: He ﷺ gave that reply three times. Then the angel recited the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (Bukhari 3).
tf.tf-quran-05.q: The surahs of the Quran are arranged in the order in which they were revealed.
tf.tf-quran-05.x: The first verses ever revealed, 'Read in the name of your Lord who created', open Surah Al-Alaq, which is Surah 96 of 114 in the mushaf (Bukhari 4953).
tf.tf-quran-06.q: The reward for reciting the Quran is counted per verse, not per letter.
tf.tf-quran-06.x: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever recites a letter of the Quran gets a good deed, multiplied by ten: 'Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter' (Tirmidhi 2910, graded Sahih).
tf.tf-quran-07.q: The Prophet ﷺ compared a believer who recites the Quran to a citron, a fruit that tastes good and smells good.
tf.tf-quran-07.x: He ﷺ said the one who recites the Quran is like a citron, good in taste and scent, while a believer who does not recite it is like a date: sweet, but with no scent (Bukhari 5020).
tf.tf-quran-08.q: The Prophet ﷺ said that Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to the whole Quran.
tf.tf-quran-08.x: He ﷺ said: 'By Him in Whose Hand my life is, this surah is equal to one third of the Quran' (Bukhari 5013).
tf.tf-quran-09.q: The Prophet ﷺ called Al-Baqarah and Al Imran 'the two bright ones' that will plead for their reciters on the Day of Resurrection.
tf.tf-quran-09.x: He ﷺ said: recite the Quran, for it will come as an intercessor for its companions. The two bright ones will come like two clouds, two shades or two flocks of birds, pleading for them (Muslim 804).
tf.tf-quran-10.q: The Quran is made up of 114 surahs.
tf.tf-quran-10.x: The Quran has 114 surahs, from Al-Fatihah (Surah 1) to An-Nas (Surah 114), the last surah in the mushaf.
tf.tf-quran-11.q: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah in the Quran, with 286 ayat.
tf.tf-quran-11.x: Al-Baqarah (The Cow, Surah 2) has 286 ayat in the standard mushaf, more than any other surah.
tf.tf-quran-12.q: Al-Ikhlas is the shortest surah in the Quran.
tf.tf-quran-12.x: The shortest is Al-Kawthar (Surah 108): just ten Arabic words in three short ayat. Al-Ikhlas has four ayat.
tf.tf-quran-13.q: Every surah of the Quran begins with Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim.
tf.tf-quran-13.x: At-Tawbah (Surah 9) is the only surah that does not begin with the basmala; it opens directly with its first ayah (Quran 9:1). All the other 113 surahs open with it.
tf.tf-quran-14.q: Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim appears in the middle of Surah An-Naml, in the letter of Prophet Sulayman.
tf.tf-quran-14.x: Sulayman's letter to the Queen of Sheba began: 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful' (Quran 27:30). It is the only basmala in the middle of a surah.
tf.tf-quran-15.q: The Quran asks: 'Do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?'
tf.tf-quran-15.x: Allah asks this in Quran 47:24. He also calls it a blessed Book sent down so that they might reflect upon its verses and those of understanding be reminded (38:29).
tf.tf-give-02.q: The Prophet ﷺ would eat some dates before going out on Eid al-Fitr, and he ate them in an odd number.
tf.tf-give-02.x: Anas (RA) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet ﷺ would not go out on the day of Eid al-Fitr until he had eaten some dates, and that he ate them in odd numbers.
tf.tf-give-03.q: The Prophet ﷺ prescribed zakat al-fitr for adults only, not for young children.
tf.tf-give-03.x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet ﷺ prescribed zakat al-fitr, a sa' (a set measure) of dates or of barley, on every Muslim: male or female, young or old.
tf.tf-give-04.q: On Eid, the Prophet ﷺ returned from the prayer by the same route he had taken to get there.
tf.tf-give-04.x: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that on the day of Eid the Prophet ﷺ would return by a different route from the one he went by.
tf.tf-give-05.q: The Prophet ﷺ ordered zakat al-fitr to be paid after the Eid prayer is over.
tf.tf-give-05.x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet ﷺ ordered zakat al-fitr to be paid before the people go out to the Eid prayer.
tf.tf-give-06.q: In the ayah on fasting Ramadan, Allah says He wants us to complete the count of days and proclaim His greatness for guiding us.
tf.tf-give-06.x: Quran 2:185: Allah wants you 'to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that to which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.' The Arabic verb here, litukabbiru, shares its root with takbir.
tf.tf-give-07.q: Zakat al-fitr purifies the fasting person from idle and indecent talk, and it is food for the poor.
tf.tf-give-07.x: Ibn Abbas (RA) said the Prophet ﷺ prescribed it to purify the fasting person from idle and obscene talk and to feed the needy. Paid before the Eid prayer, it is accepted as zakat (Abu Dawud, hasan).
tf.tf-give-08.q: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged fasting on the day of Eid al-Fitr as a way to thank Allah for Ramadan.
tf.tf-give-08.x: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Umar (RA) said at Eid that the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on two days: the day you break from your fasting (Eid al-Fitr) and the day you eat from your sacrifices (Eid al-Adha).
tf.tf-give-09.q: In Islam, only giving money or goods counts as sadaqah (charity).
tf.tf-give-09.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Every act of goodness is sadaqah' (Sahih Muslim). Charity is not limited to money: every good deed counts.
tf.tf-give-10.q: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, he said Allah had replaced the people's two pre-Islamic days of play with better ones: Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr.
tf.tf-give-10.x: Anas (RA) said the people of Madinah had two days of play from before Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah had given them better: the day of sacrifice and the day of breaking the fast (Abu Dawud, sahih).
tf.tf-give-11.q: One of the seven kinds of people Allah will shade on the Day when there is no shade but His is someone who gives charity in secret.
tf.tf-give-11.x: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ lists seven kinds of people Allah will shade on the Day of Judgment, including one who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives.
tf.tf-give-12.q: The Prophet ﷺ gave the Eid sermon (khutbah) first and then led the Eid prayer.
tf.tf-give-12.x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and Umar used to pray the two Eid prayers before the sermon (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).
tf.tf-give-13.q: Reminding people of the charity you gave them has no effect on its reward.
tf.tf-give-13.x: Allah says: 'O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury' (Quran 2:264). Give for Allah's sake and do not remind people of it.
tf.tf-give-14.q: The Prophet ﷺ had the adhan and iqamah called for the Eid prayer, just as for the five daily prayers.
tf.tf-give-14.x: Jabir ibn Samurah (RA) said he prayed the two Eid prayers with the Prophet ﷺ more than once or twice, without any adhan or iqamah (Sahih Muslim).
tf.tf-give-15.q: The Quran likens spending in Allah's way to a seed that grows seven ears of grain, each holding a hundred grains.
tf.tf-give-15.x: Quran 2:261 gives this parable for those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, and adds that Allah multiplies the reward for whom He wills.
tf.tf-hist-01.q: Allah says in Surah al-Qadr that He sent down the Quran on Laylatul Qadr, the Night of Decree.
tf.tf-hist-01.x: Surah al-Qadr begins: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree' (Quran 97:1). Quran 2:185 names Ramadan as the month in which the Quran was revealed.
tf.tf-hist-02.q: The first verses revealed to the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Hira were from Surah al-Fatihah.
tf.tf-hist-02.x: In the Cave of Hira the angel brought the opening of Surah al-Alaq: 'Recite in the name of your Lord who created' (Quran 96:1), as Aishah narrates in Bukhari 3.
tf.tf-hist-03.q: The Battle of Badr was fought in Ramadan, and the Quran calls it 'the day of criterion'.
tf.tf-hist-03.x: Historians record that Badr was fought in Ramadan of 2 AH. Quran 8:41 calls it 'the day of criterion, the day when the two armies met.'
tf.tf-hist-04.q: At the Battle of Badr, the Muslim army outnumbered the army of Quraysh.
tf.tf-hist-04.x: Umar reports that the polytheists numbered a thousand and the Muslims 319 (Muslim 1763). Quran 3:123 recalls that Allah gave them victory at Badr 'while you were weak'.
tf.tf-hist-05.q: The Conquest of Makkah took place in the month of Ramadan.
tf.tf-hist-05.x: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet ﷺ made the expedition of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan (Bukhari 4275). This was in the year 8 AH.
tf.tf-hist-06.q: The Prophet ﷺ set out to conquer Makkah with an army of only about a thousand men.
tf.tf-hist-06.x: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet ﷺ left Madinah for Makkah in Ramadan with ten thousand people (Bukhari 4276).
tf.tf-hist-07.q: In the year he passed away, the Prophet ﷺ observed i'tikaf for twenty days instead of his usual ten.
tf.tf-hist-07.x: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ observed i'tikaf for ten days every Ramadan, and for twenty days in the year he passed away (Bukhari 2044).
tf.tf-hist-08.q: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, his wives no longer observed i'tikaf.
tf.tf-hist-08.x: Aishah reports that he observed i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan until Allah took him, and then his wives observed i'tikaf after him (Bukhari 2026).
tf.tf-hist-09.q: Every year, Jibreel reviewed the Quran with the Prophet ﷺ twice.
tf.tf-hist-09.x: Abu Hurayrah reports that Jibreel reviewed the Quran with the Prophet ﷺ once a year, but twice in the year he passed away (Bukhari 4998).
tf.tf-hist-10.q: When Aishah asked Fatimah what the Prophet ﷺ had told her in secret, Fatimah would not reveal it while he was alive.
tf.tf-hist-10.x: She refused to disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. After he passed away she told Aishah: Jibreel had reviewed the Quran with him twice in his last year, which he saw as a sign his death was near (Bukhari 3624).
tf.tf-hist-11.q: On his journey to Makkah in Ramadan, the Prophet ﷺ was fasting at first and then broke his fast on the way.
tf.tf-hist-11.x: Ibn Abbas reports that he set out for Makkah in Ramadan fasting, then broke his fast at al-Kadid, and the people broke theirs too (Bukhari 1944). Quran 2:185 lets travellers make up the days later.
tf.tf-hist-12.q: When the Companions travelled with the Prophet ﷺ in Ramadan, those who fasted criticised those who did not.
tf.tf-hist-12.x: Anas reports that when they travelled with the Prophet ﷺ in Ramadan, those fasting did not find fault with those not fasting, nor the other way round (Muslim 1118).
tf.tf-prep-01.q: Outside Ramadan, Sha'ban was the month the Prophet ﷺ fasted the least, to save his strength for Ramadan.
tf.tf-prep-01.x: Aisha (RA) said she never saw him fast a whole month except Ramadan, and never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban (Bukhari 1969, Muslim 1156).
tf.tf-prep-02.q: When breaking his fast, the Prophet ﷺ would say: 'Thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.'
tf.tf-prep-02.x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported that he ﷺ said this when he broke his fast: Dhahaba al-zama'u wabtallat al-'uruqu wa thabata al-ajru in sha' Allah (Abu Dawud 2357).
tf.tf-prep-03.q: The Prophet ﷺ said Sha'ban is a month people neglect, in which deeds are raised to Allah, and he loved to be fasting when his deeds were raised.
tf.tf-prep-03.x: When Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) noted how much he fasted in Sha'ban, he ﷺ called it a neglected month between Rajab and Ramadan in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds (Nasa'i 2357).
tf.tf-prep-04.q: The Quran's verses about fasting in Surah al-Baqarah do not mention dua at all.
tf.tf-prep-04.x: Among the fasting verses (2:183-187), Allah says: 'Indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me' (Quran 2:186).
tf.tf-prep-05.q: Aisha (RA) said there were times she could only make up her missed Ramadan fasts in Sha'ban.
tf.tf-prep-05.x: Aisha (RA) said she would owe fasts from Ramadan and could not make them up except in the month of Sha'ban (Bukhari 1950, Muslim 1146).
tf.tf-prep-06.q: Sayyid al-Istighfar, the 'master' supplication for forgiveness, is simply the word 'Astaghfirullah'.
tf.tf-prep-06.x: It is a longer dua the Prophet ﷺ taught, beginning: 'Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduka...' (O Allah, You are my Lord...) (Bukhari 6306).
tf.tf-prep-07.q: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged fasting a day or two just before Ramadan to get ready for it.
tf.tf-prep-07.x: He said none of you should fast a day or two before Ramadan, unless it is a fast that person regularly keeps, in which case he may fast that day (Bukhari 1914, Muslim 1082).
tf.tf-prep-08.q: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says Sayyid al-Istighfar, the master dua for forgiveness, by day with firm faith and dies before evening is among the people of Paradise.
tf.tf-prep-08.x: He said whoever says it with firm faith during the day and dies before evening, or at night and dies before morning, will be among the people of Paradise (Bukhari 6306).
tf.tf-prep-09.q: When people asked the Prophet ﷺ about the crescent moons, Allah told him to say they are measurements of time for people and for Hajj.
tf.tf-prep-09.x: Allah says: 'They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj' (Quran 2:189). Islamic months, including Ramadan, follow the moon.
tf.tf-prep-10.q: The dua the Prophet ﷺ made most often asked only for good in the Hereafter, not in this world.
tf.tf-prep-10.x: Anas (RA) said his most frequent dua was: 'O Allah, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire' (Bukhari 6389, Muslim 2690).
tf.tf-prep-11.x: The Prophet ﷺ indicated with his hands that a month is sometimes 29 days and sometimes 30 (Bukhari 1913, Muslim 1080), so Ramadan can also be 29 days.
tf.tf-prep-12.q: The Prophet ﷺ said a person's dua is answered as long as they do not become impatient and say, 'I made dua but was not answered.'
tf.tf-prep-12.x: He said the dua of any of you is answered as long as he is not hasty, saying 'I made dua but was not answered' (Bukhari 6340). A version in Muslim adds: as long as he does not ask for sin or cutting family ties (Muslim 2735).
tf.tf-prep-13.q: The Prophet ﷺ told people to take on only as many good deeds as they are able to do.
tf.tf-prep-13.x: Asked which deeds Allah loves most, he said the most regular ones, even if few, and added: take on only the deeds that are within your ability (Bukhari 6465, Muslim 782).
tf.tf-prep-14.q: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged saying 'O Allah, forgive me if You wish' to show humility in dua.
tf.tf-prep-14.x: He said none of you should say 'O Allah, forgive me if You wish'. Ask with firm resolve, for no one can force Allah (Bukhari 6339, Muslim 2679).
tf.tf-prep-15.q: Whenever the Prophet's ﷺ household began a good deed, they would keep it up.
tf.tf-prep-15.x: Aisha (RA) reported that whenever the family of Muhammad ﷺ did a deed, they would keep it up regularly (Muslim 782).
mcq.mcq-a-01.q: Anas (RA) described what the Prophet ﷺ broke his fast with before praying. What was his order of preference?
mcq.mcq-a-01.o0: Water, then dried dates, then fresh dates
mcq.mcq-a-01.o1: Milk, then fresh dates, then bread
mcq.mcq-a-01.o2: Fresh dates, then dried dates, then water
mcq.mcq-a-01.o3: Dried dates, then milk, then water
mcq.mcq-a-01.x: He ﷺ broke his fast with fresh dates (rutab) before praying; if there were none, with dried dates; and if there were none, with a few sips of water.
mcq.mcq-a-02.q: The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) to fast three days each month. He said that is like fasting for how long?
mcq.mcq-a-02.x: He ﷺ said: Fast three days a month, for a good deed is rewarded ten times over, and that is like fasting the whole year. A simple way to keep fasting after Ramadan.
mcq.mcq-a-03.q: Quran 2:183 tells the believers that fasting has been prescribed for them. How does the verse end: 'so that you may...'?
mcq.mcq-a-03.x: The verse ends 'la'allakum tattaqun': so that you may become righteous, gaining taqwa (mindfulness of Allah). The Quran names this as the purpose of fasting.
mcq.mcq-a-04.q: In Quran 2:187, believers may eat and drink at night until what becomes distinct to them?
mcq.mcq-a-04.o0: The first rays of the rising sun
mcq.mcq-a-04.o1: The white thread of dawn from the black thread
mcq.mcq-a-04.o2: The last light of the moon
mcq.mcq-a-04.x: Allah says: Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of night. Then complete the fast until the night.
mcq.mcq-a-05.q: The Prophet ﷺ said the fasting person has two joys. One is when he breaks his fast. When is the other?
mcq.mcq-a-05.x: There are two joys for the fasting person: one when he breaks his fast, and one when he meets his Lord, when he will be pleased because of his fasting.
mcq.mcq-a-06.q: The Prophet ﷺ spoke of gates of Paradise for the people of prayer, fasting and charity. Abu Bakr (RA) asked if anyone is called from all of them. What was the reply?
mcq.mcq-a-06.o0: No, each person has only one gate
mcq.mcq-a-06.o1: Yes, and I hope you will be one of them
mcq.mcq-a-06.o3: Only those who fasted every day
mcq.mcq-a-06.x: Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that the people of fasting will be called from the gate of ar-Rayyan. When Abu Bakr (RA) asked about all the gates, he ﷺ said: Yes, and I hope you will be one of them.
mcq.mcq-a-07.q: The Prophet ﷺ said people will remain upon goodness as long as they do what?
mcq.mcq-a-07.o1: Delay iftar until the stars appear
mcq.mcq-a-07.x: Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: The people will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten to break the fast. So do not delay iftar once its time has come.
mcq.mcq-a-08.q: Ibn Abbas (RA) said the Prophet ﷺ prescribed zakat al-fitr as a purification for the fasting person from what?
mcq.mcq-a-08.x: He ﷺ prescribed it to purify the fasting person from idle and obscene talk, and as food for the poor. Given before the Eid prayer, it is accepted as zakat.
mcq.mcq-a-09.q: The Prophet ﷺ said prayer in congregation is superior to praying alone by how many degrees?
mcq.mcq-a-09.x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees superior to prayer offered by a person alone.
mcq.mcq-a-10.q: The Prophet ﷺ asked: if a river ran by your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain? What was he describing?
mcq.mcq-a-10.x: The Companions said no dirt would remain. He ﷺ said: That is the example of the five prayers, with which Allah wipes away sins.
mcq.mcq-a-11.q: In Ramadan, more and more people gathered to pray behind the Prophet ﷺ at night. Why did he then stop coming out to them?
mcq.mcq-a-11.o0: He was too ill to lead them
mcq.mcq-a-11.o1: He feared it would be made obligatory
mcq.mcq-a-11.o3: He was away on a journey
mcq.mcq-a-11.x: Aishah (RA) reported he said: I saw what you did, and nothing stopped me from coming out to you except that I feared it would be made obligatory on you. That was in Ramadan.
mcq.mcq-a-12.q: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ for his company in Paradise. What did the Prophet ﷺ tell him to do to help reach it?
mcq.mcq-a-12.x: Rabi'ah (RA), who brought him water for wudu at night, said: I ask for your company in Paradise. He ﷺ said: Then help me to achieve this for you by making many prostrations.
mcq.mcq-a-13.q: Which prayer did the Prophet ﷺ call the best prayer after the obligatory prayers?
mcq.mcq-a-13.x: Abu Hurairah (RA) reported: The best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month, Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the prayer at night.
mcq.mcq-a-14.q: The Prophet ﷺ would stand in night prayer until his feet swelled. When asked why, what did he say?
mcq.mcq-a-14.o0: I like the quiet of the night
mcq.mcq-a-14.o1: Should I not be a thankful servant?
mcq.mcq-a-14.o2: I want to finish the whole Quran
mcq.mcq-a-14.o3: The angels told me to do so
mcq.mcq-a-14.x: Al-Mughirah (RA) reported that he prayed until his feet swelled, and when asked about it he said: Should I not be a thankful servant?
mcq.mcq-a-15.q: The first thing a person will be brought to account for is the prayer. If their obligatory prayers are lacking, what completes them?
mcq.mcq-a-15.x: Allah will say: See whether My servant has any voluntary prayers. If he has, the obligatory prayers are completed with them. A strong reason to keep up the Sunnah prayers.
mcq.mcq-a-16.q: Quran 29:45 says prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. What does the verse then say is greater?
mcq.mcq-a-16.x: Allah says: Establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
mcq.mcq-a-17.q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest surah in the Quran?
mcq.mcq-a-17.x: He ﷺ told Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla (RA) that Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'alamin is the greatest surah: the seven oft-repeated verses and the Grand Quran given to him.
mcq.mcq-a-18.q: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) which verse in the Book of Allah is the greatest. Which verse did Ubayy name?
mcq.mcq-a-18.x: Ubayy (RA), known as Abu al-Mundhir, answered: Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. The Prophet ﷺ tapped him on the chest and said: May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir.
mcq.mcq-a-19.q: A man heard someone repeating Surah al-Ikhlas over and over and told the Prophet ﷺ, as if he thought it too little. What did the Prophet ﷺ say it is equal to?
mcq.mcq-a-19.x: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: By Him in Whose Hand my soul is, it is equal to one-third of the Quran.
mcq.mcq-a-20.q: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever recites a letter of Allah's Book earns a good deed. How many times is that good deed multiplied?
mcq.mcq-a-20.x: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported: each good deed is multiplied by ten. I do not say Alif Lam Mim is one letter; Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter.
mcq.mcq-a-21.q: The Prophet ﷺ likened the believer who recites the Quran to a citron (utrujjah). Why a citron?
mcq.mcq-a-21.o2: It tastes good and smells good
mcq.mcq-a-21.x: Abu Musa (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: the believer who recites the Quran is like a citron, good in smell and taste; the believer who does not recite it is like a date, sweet but without smell.
mcq.mcq-a-22.q: How long did the Prophet ﷺ first tell Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) to take to recite the whole Quran?
mcq.mcq-a-22.x: He ﷺ said: Recite the whole Quran in one month. When Abdullah said he had strength for more, he said: Then recite it in seven days.
mcq.mcq-a-23.q: A man reciting Surah al-Kahf saw a cloud come closer and closer over him, and his horse grew restless. What did the Prophet ﷺ say it was?
mcq.mcq-a-23.o0: A storm cloud about to burst
mcq.mcq-a-23.o1: Dust stirred up by the desert wind
mcq.mcq-a-23.o2: Tranquility sent down with the Quran
mcq.mcq-a-23.x: Al-Bara (RA) reported that the man told the Prophet ﷺ about it the next morning, and he said: That was the sakinah (tranquility), which came down because of the Quran.
mcq.mcq-a-24.q: Which of these statements does Allah repeat four times in Surah al-Qamar?
mcq.mcq-a-24.o0: The Quran was sent down in Ramadan
mcq.mcq-a-24.o1: We have made the Quran easy for remembrance
mcq.mcq-a-24.o2: The Quran is healing for the believers
mcq.mcq-a-24.o3: Recite the Quran with measured recitation
mcq.mcq-a-24.x: Allah says in 54:17, 22, 32 and 40: And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
mcq.mcq-a-25.q: Surah al-Qadr says the Night of Decree is peace until when?
mcq.mcq-a-25.o1: The last third of the night
mcq.mcq-a-25.x: Allah says: Peace it is until the emergence of dawn (97:5). The night stays a night of peace until Fajr breaks, so keep striving until then.
mcq.mcq-a-26.q: According to Surah al-Qadr, who descend on the Night of Decree by permission of their Lord?
mcq.mcq-a-26.x: Allah says: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter (97:4). The Spirit here is Jibreel.
mcq.mcq-a-27.q: Surah al-Qadr says the Quran was sent down on the Night of Decree. Which other surah says it was sent down 'during a blessed night'?
mcq.mcq-a-27.x: Allah says in Surah ad-Dukhan: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night (44:3), and in Surah al-Qadr: We sent it down during the Night of Decree (97:1).
mcq.mcq-a-28.q: The Prophet ﷺ came out to tell the people the date of Laylatul Qadr, but knowledge of it was taken away. Why?
mcq.mcq-a-28.o3: He was called away on a journey
mcq.mcq-a-28.x: He ﷺ said: I came out to tell you about Laylatul Qadr, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was taken away, and perhaps that is better for you.
mcq.mcq-a-29.q: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) mentioned a sign the Prophet ﷺ gave for the morning after Laylatul Qadr. What is it?
mcq.mcq-a-29.o0: The sun rises white, without rays
mcq.mcq-a-29.o1: A red moon rises at dawn
mcq.mcq-a-29.x: Ubayy (RA) said the sign the Prophet ﷺ told them of is that the sun rises on the morning after it white, without rays.
mcq.mcq-a-30.q: Abu Hurairah (RA) said the Prophet ﷺ used to do i'tikaf for ten days every Ramadan. How many days did he do in the year he passed away?
mcq.mcq-a-30.x: Abu Hurairah (RA) said he ﷺ used to do i'tikaf for ten days every Ramadan, and in the year he passed away he did i'tikaf for twenty days.
mcq.mcq-a-31.q: Seeking Laylatul Qadr, the Prophet ﷺ did i'tikaf in the first ten days of Ramadan, then the middle ten. What was he then told?
mcq.mcq-a-31.o0: It is in the month of Shawwal
mcq.mcq-a-31.o1: It is in the last ten nights
mcq.mcq-a-31.o2: It is on the first night
mcq.mcq-a-31.o3: It is on the night of Eid
mcq.mcq-a-31.x: Abu Sa'id (RA) reported he said: I did i'tikaf in the first ten seeking this night, then in the middle ten. Then I was told it is in the last ten.
mcq.mcq-a-32.q: During i'tikaf in the masjid, the Prophet ﷺ would lean his head into the house to Aishah (RA). Why?
mcq.mcq-a-32.o2: To see if the moon had risen
mcq.mcq-a-32.o3: So she could comb his hair
mcq.mcq-a-32.x: Aishah (RA) said: he would put his head in to me while he was in the masjid, and I would comb his hair. In i'tikaf he would not enter the house except for a need.
mcq.mcq-b-01.q: Complete the hadith: 'Save yourself from the Fire, even by giving half of a ... in charity.'
mcq.mcq-b-01.x: Adi ibn Hatim heard the Prophet ﷺ say this. No charity is too small: even half a date given in charity can help protect you from the Fire.
mcq.mcq-b-02.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The upper hand is better than the lower hand.' Which is the upper hand?
mcq.mcq-b-02.x: Ibn Umar heard him say this on the pulpit while speaking about charity and not begging: the upper hand is the one that gives, and the lower hand is the one that asks.
mcq.mcq-b-03.q: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ which charity carries the greatest reward. What did he answer?
mcq.mcq-b-03.o0: Giving while healthy and fearing poverty
mcq.mcq-b-03.o1: A large gift left in a will at death
mcq.mcq-b-03.o2: Giving only once you are rich
mcq.mcq-b-03.x: Give while you are healthy, keen to keep your wealth, fearing poverty and hoping to be rich. Do not delay until death approaches and then say: give this much to so-and-so.
mcq.mcq-b-04.q: Of a dinar spent in Allah's path, on freeing a slave, on a needy person or on your family, which did the Prophet ﷺ say has the greatest reward?
mcq.mcq-b-04.o0: The one spent in Allah's path
mcq.mcq-b-04.o1: The one spent freeing a slave
mcq.mcq-b-04.o2: The one given to a needy person
mcq.mcq-b-04.o3: The one spent on your family
mcq.mcq-b-04.x: Abu Hurairah reported that of these four, the dinar with the greatest reward is the one you spend on your family. Providing for your family is itself a rewarded deed.
mcq.mcq-b-05.q: When 'Never will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love' (3:92) was revealed, what did Abu Talhah give in charity?
mcq.mcq-b-05.x: Bayruha, facing the Prophet's mosque, was the property Abu Talhah loved most. He gave it for Allah's sake, and on the advice of the Prophet ﷺ he divided it among his relatives.
mcq.mcq-b-06.q: Nu'man ibn Bashir reported which two surahs the Prophet ﷺ recited in the two Eid prayers and the Friday prayer. Which were they?
mcq.mcq-b-06.x: He recited al-A'la and al-Ghashiyah in both Eid prayers and in the Friday prayer. Abu Waqid al-Laythi also reported him reciting Qaf and al-Qamar on Eid (Muslim 891).
mcq.mcq-b-07.q: Umm Atiyyah said women, even those menstruating, were told to come out on Eid day. What did they do there?
mcq.mcq-b-07.o0: Said takbir and made dua with the people
mcq.mcq-b-07.o2: Cooked the Eid meal for everyone
mcq.mcq-b-07.x: They stayed behind the people, saying takbir and supplicating with them, hoping for the blessing and purification of that day. Menstruating women kept away from the prayer area (Bukhari 974).
mcq.mcq-b-08.q: After the Eid al-Fitr prayer, the Prophet ﷺ went to the women with Bilal and told them to give charity. What did they give?
mcq.mcq-b-08.x: Ibn Abbas reports that after praying two rak'ahs on the day of Fitr, the Prophet ﷺ went to the women with Bilal and ordered charity, and they began giving their earrings and necklaces.
mcq.mcq-b-09.q: On Eid al-Adha, what did the Prophet ﷺ say is the first thing we do on this day?
mcq.mcq-b-09.x: Al-Bara heard him say in his khutbah: the first thing we do on this day is pray, then we return and sacrifice; whoever does that has followed our Sunnah. Eating dates before going out is for Eid al-Fitr (Bukhari 953).
mcq.mcq-b-10.q: How much zakat al-fitr in dates or barley did the Prophet ﷺ make due for each Muslim?
mcq.mcq-b-10.x: Ibn Umar reports he made it one sa' (a measure of volume) of dates or barley for every Muslim, slave or free, male or female, young or old, paid before the Eid prayer.
mcq.mcq-b-11.q: After the first revelation in the cave of Hira, the Prophet ﷺ came home with his heart trembling. Who comforted him, saying Allah would never disgrace him?
mcq.mcq-b-11.x: Aishah narrates that Khadijah told him Allah would never disgrace him, for he kept ties with his relatives, helped the weak and the poor, honoured guests and helped people in hardship.
mcq.mcq-b-12.q: Before fasting Ramadan was prescribed, the Prophet ﷺ fasted and told others to fast on which day?
mcq.mcq-b-12.x: Aishah said he fasted Ashura and, in Madinah, ordered others to fast it too. When fasting the month of Ramadan was prescribed, fasting Ashura became optional.
mcq.mcq-b-13.q: In the early days of fasting, what happened if a Companion fell asleep at night before eating?
mcq.mcq-b-13.o0: He had to make up the fast
mcq.mcq-b-13.o1: He could eat once he woke up
mcq.mcq-b-13.o2: He had to feed a poor person
mcq.mcq-b-13.o3: He could not eat until the next sunset
mcq.mcq-b-13.x: Al-Bara reported that Qais ibn Sirmah fell asleep before eating and fainted the next day. Then Allah revealed part of 2:187, allowing them to eat and drink through the night.
mcq.mcq-b-14.q: In which month did the Prophet ﷺ set out on the campaign of the Conquest of Makkah?
mcq.mcq-b-14.x: Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ went on the Conquest campaign in Ramadan. He fasted until he reached al-Kadid, a watering place on the way, and then broke his fast.
mcq.mcq-b-15.q: Umar (RA) saw people praying at night in Ramadan in scattered groups. Behind which reciter did he gather them?
mcq.mcq-b-15.x: Abdur-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari reports that Umar decided to unite them behind one reciter, Ubayy ibn Ka'b. On a later night he saw them praying together behind their reciter.
mcq.mcq-b-16.q: Outside Ramadan, in which month did Aishah (RA) see the Prophet ﷺ fast the most?
mcq.mcq-b-16.x: Aishah said she never saw him fast a complete month except Ramadan, and never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban, the month before Ramadan.
mcq.mcq-b-17.q: Aishah (RA) said she could only make up her missed Ramadan fasts in Sha'ban. What reason did the narrator Yahya give?
mcq.mcq-b-17.o1: She was busy with the Prophet ﷺ
mcq.mcq-b-17.o3: She travelled most of the year
mcq.mcq-b-17.x: Aishah sometimes owed days from Ramadan and made them up in Sha'ban; the narrator Yahya explained she was occupied with the Prophet ﷺ. A reminder to plan any make-up fasts before Ramadan.
mcq.mcq-b-18.q: The Prophet ﷺ said none of you should fast a day or two just before Ramadan, except whom?
mcq.mcq-b-18.o1: Those who feel strong and healthy
mcq.mcq-b-18.x: Abu Hurairah reported: do not fast a day or two before Ramadan, unless it is a fast that a person regularly keeps; then he may fast that day.
mcq.mcq-b-19.q: In Quran 2:185, among the verses on fasting Ramadan, what does Allah say He intends for you?
mcq.mcq-b-19.x: 'Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship.' In the same verse, whoever is ill or on a journey may fast an equal number of other days instead.
mcq.mcq-b-20.q: The Prophet ﷺ said that when Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of the Fire are closed. What happens to the devils?
mcq.mcq-b-20.x: Abu Hurairah reported: when Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed and the devils are chained. Make the most of this blessed month.
mcq.mcq-b-21.q: In Quran 2:186, set among the verses on fasting, what does Allah say when His servants ask about Him?
mcq.mcq-b-21.x: 'Indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, that they may be rightly guided.'
mcq.mcq-b-22.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Dua is ...' What completes this short hadith?
mcq.mcq-b-22.x: An-Nu'man ibn Bashir reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Dua is worship,' and then recited: 'And your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you' (Quran 40:60).
mcq.mcq-b-23.q: According to Anas, which dua did the Prophet ﷺ make most often?
mcq.mcq-b-23.o0: Our Lord, give us good in this world and the next
mcq.mcq-b-23.o1: My Lord, increase me in knowledge
mcq.mcq-b-23.o3: My Lord, forgive me and my parents
mcq.mcq-b-23.x: His most frequent dua was: 'O Allah, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire' (also Quran 2:201).
mcq.mcq-b-24.q: Which Prophet called out from the belly of the whale: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers'?
mcq.mcq-b-24.x: This is the dua of Dhun-Nun, Prophet Yunus. The Prophet ﷺ said no Muslim calls on Allah with it for anything except that Allah responds to him.
mcq.mcq-b-25.q: The Prophet ﷺ said your dua will be answered as long as you do not do what?
mcq.mcq-b-25.o1: Say impatiently: 'I made dua but got no answer'
mcq.mcq-b-25.x: Abu Hurairah reported: the dua of any of you is answered as long as he is not hasty, saying, 'I called upon Allah but was not answered.' Keep asking with patience.
mcq.mcq-b-26.q: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'Advise me!' and repeated it several times. What did the Prophet ﷺ say each time?
mcq.mcq-b-26.x: Abu Hurairah reported that each time the man asked again, the Prophet ﷺ gave the same answer: 'Do not become angry.'
mcq.mcq-b-27.q: The Prophet ﷺ tied three manners to belief in Allah and the Last Day: speaking good or keeping silent, honouring guests, and what else?
mcq.mcq-b-27.x: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbour, should honour his guest, and should speak good or keep quiet.
mcq.mcq-b-28.q: Quran 3:134 praises those who spend in ease and hardship and who restrain their anger. What else do they do?
mcq.mcq-b-28.o3: Remember every wrong done to them
mcq.mcq-b-28.x: 'Who spend in ease and hardship, who restrain anger and who pardon the people, and Allah loves the doers of good.' Holding back anger and forgiving go together.
mcq.mcq-b-29.q: Complete the hadith: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he ...'
mcq.mcq-b-29.x: Anas reported this hadith. Complete faith means wanting good for others just as you want it for yourself.
mcq.mcq-b-30.q: The Prophet ﷺ said truthfulness leads to righteousness. What did he say righteousness leads to?
mcq.mcq-b-30.x: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported: truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise; a person keeps telling the truth until he becomes truthful. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness to the Fire.
fc.fc-vocab-01.b: Fasting: refraining from food, drink and marital relations from dawn until sunset for Allah's sake. The Quran says to eat and drink until dawn, then complete the fast until night.
fc.fc-vocab-02.b: The pre-dawn meal eaten before a day of fasting. The Prophet ﷺ said: Take suhoor, for in suhoor there is blessing.
fc.fc-vocab-03.b: Breaking the fast at sunset, and the meal eaten then. The Prophet ﷺ said that when night comes, day departs and the sun has set, the fasting person breaks the fast.
fc.fc-vocab-04.b: Intention: the aim in the heart behind an action. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever goes to bed intending to pray at night but is overcome by sleep until morning has what he intended recorded for him.
fc.fc-vocab-05.b: Mindfulness of Allah that guards a person from what displeases Him. Allah prescribed fasting for us, as for those before us, so that we may attain taqwa.
fc.fc-vocab-06.b: The night prayer of Ramadan; the name means 'rests', from the pauses between sets of rak'ahs. The Prophet ﷺ led it in the mosque for a few nights, then stopped, fearing it would be made obligatory.
fc.fc-vocab-07.b: Standing in prayer at night: spending part of the night in voluntary prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer at night.
fc.fc-vocab-08.b: Voluntary prayer at night; the word carries the sense of giving up sleep to pray. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to pray part of the night with the Quran as extra worship for him.
fc.fc-vocab-09.b: Literally 'odd'. The odd-numbered prayer that ends the night's prayers; the Prophet ﷺ said it makes what one has prayed at night odd.
fc.fc-vocab-10.b: Staying in the mosque for a time, devoted to worship. The Quran mentions believers who are 'staying for worship in the mosques'.
fc.fc-vocab-11.b: The Night of Decree (or Power), a night in Ramadan in which the Quran was sent down. Allah says: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.
fc.fc-vocab-12.b: The charity of breaking the fast, given at the end of Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ made it due for every Muslim, young or old, and ordered it paid before the Eid prayer.
fc.fc-vocab-13.b: Charity given for Allah's sake, especially voluntary giving. The Prophet ﷺ said: every act of kindness is sadaqah.
fc.fc-vocab-14.b: Literally 'ransom': feeding a needy person in place of fasts one cannot keep or make up later. Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly unable to fast, who feed one needy person for each day.
fc.fc-vocab-15.b: Making up a missed act of worship later, such as missed Ramadan fasts. Aishah (RA) said women were ordered to make up fasts missed during menstruation, but not prayers.
fc.fc-vocab-16.b: Reciting the Quran correctly, giving each letter its due sound and following the rules of recitation. Allah says: recite the Quran with measured recitation.
fc.fc-vocab-17.b: Completing a full reading of the Quran from beginning to end. The Prophet ﷺ advised Abdullah ibn Amr to complete it once a month.
fc.fc-vocab-18.b: A chapter of the Quran; there are 114 surahs. Allah challenges anyone in doubt about the Quran to produce a single surah like it.
fc.fc-vocab-19.b: A verse of the Quran. The word also means 'sign': Allah says that in the creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day there are signs for people of understanding.
fc.fc-vocab-20.b: Supplication: calling upon Allah and asking Him directly. Allah says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
fc.fc-vocab-21.b: Remembrance of Allah, in the heart and on the tongue. Allah says: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
fc.fc-vocab-22.b: Asking Allah for forgiveness, as in saying Astaghfirullah. Prophet Nuh told his people: Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.
fc.fc-vocab-23.b: Repentance: turning back to Allah after a sin. Allah says: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance.
fc.fc-vocab-24.b: Self-accounting: honestly reviewing one's own deeds. Allah says: let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.
fc.fc-vocab-25.b: The month just before Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ fasted more in Sha'ban than in any other month apart from Ramadan.
fc.fc-vocab-26.b: The festival of breaking the fast that marks the end of Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ would not go out on its morning until he had eaten some dates.
fc.fc-vocab-27.b: Saying Allahu Akbar, 'Allah is the Greatest'. In the fasting verses, Allah says He wants us to complete the count of days and proclaim His greatness for guiding us.
fc.fc-vocab-28.b: The way of the Prophet ﷺ: his teachings and practice; also used for recommended acts. To men set on nonstop prayer and fasting, he said: I fast and break my fast, I pray and sleep... whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.
fc.fc-vocab-29.b: An obligatory duty. A man asked what Allah had made obligatory for him in prayer and fasting; the Prophet ﷺ named the five daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan, saying anything more is voluntary.
fc.fc-vocab-30.b: One unit of the prayer, made up of standing, bowing and prostrating. The Prophet ﷺ said: when you enter the mosque, pray two rak'ahs before sitting.
fc.fc-dua-01.f: When breaking your fast at iftar
fc.fc-dua-01.b: The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
fc.fc-dua-02.f: If you come upon Laylatul Qadr - taught by the Prophet ﷺ to Aishah
fc.fc-dua-02.b: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
fc.fc-dua-03.f: By day or by night, with firm faith: Sayyid al-Istighfar, the best way to seek forgiveness
fc.fc-dua-03.b: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, keeping Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
fc.fc-dua-04.f: After eating at someone's home: the dua the Prophet ﷺ made for his host
fc.fc-dua-04.b: May fasting people break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels send blessings upon you.
fc.fc-dua-05.f: Any time: the dua the Prophet ﷺ made most often (Bukhari 6389)
fc.fc-dua-05.b: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
fc.fc-dua-06.f: Asking Allah to keep your heart firm on guidance
fc.fc-dua-06.b: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
fc.fc-dua-07.f: For your parents: Allah tells us in the Quran to say this
fc.fc-dua-07.b: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.
fc.fc-dua-08.f: When seeking knowledge: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to say this
fc.fc-dua-08.b: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
fc.fc-dua-09.f: Asking Allah to accept a good deed: said by Ibrahim and Ismail while building the Ka'bah
fc.fc-dua-09.b: Our Lord, accept this from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
fc.fc-dua-10.f: In distress: the call of Yunus in the darkness, which Allah answered (Quran 21:88)
fc.fc-dua-10.b: There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
fc.fc-dua-11.f: For your spouse and children: a dua of the servants of the Most Merciful
fc.fc-dua-11.b: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and children comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the righteous.
fc.fc-dua-12.f: For yourself and your children to keep up prayer: a dua of Ibrahim
fc.fc-dua-12.b: My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and from my descendants too. Our Lord, accept my supplication.
fc.fc-ayah-01.f: Quran 2:183 - Fasting is prescribed, and its purpose
