fc.fc-ayah-01.b: O you who believe, fasting has been decreed for you as it was decreed for those before you, so that you may become righteous (attain taqwa).
fc.fc-ayah-02.f: Quran 2:184 - A limited number of days, and those excused
fc.fc-ayah-02.b: Fasting is for a limited number of days; whoever is ill or travelling makes up an equal number of other days. For those who can fast only with extreme difficulty, there is a ransom (fidyah): feeding a poor person. Doing more good is better, and fasting is best for you, if you only knew.
fc.fc-ayah-03.f: Quran 2:185 - The month of the Quran, and Allah wants ease for you
fc.fc-ayah-03.b: In the month of Ramadan the Quran was revealed, a guidance for people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. Whoever witnesses the month is to fast it; whoever is ill or travelling makes up an equal number of other days. Allah wants ease for you, not hardship, and wants you to complete the number of days and glorify Him for guiding you, that you may be grateful.
fc.fc-ayah-04.f: Quran 2:186 - When My servants ask you about Me
fc.fc-ayah-04.b: When Allah's servants ask about Him, He is near. He answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, so let them respond to Him and believe in Him, that they may be rightly guided.
fc.fc-ayah-05.f: Quran 2:187 - The nights of the fast, and eating until dawn (Arabic: excerpt)
fc.fc-ayah-05.b: On the nights of the fast, spouses are permitted to each other (not during i'tikaf in the mosques); they are a garment for one another. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is distinct from the black, then complete the fast until night (sunset). These are Allah's limits.
fc.fc-ayah-06.f: Quran 97:1-5 - Surah al-Qadr: the Night of Decree
fc.fc-ayah-06.b: Allah sent the Quran down on the Night of Decree, a night better than a thousand months. In it the angels and the Spirit (Jibreel) descend by their Lord's permission for every matter. It is peace until the emergence of dawn.
fc.fc-ayah-07.f: Quran 44:3 - The Book sent down on a blessed night
fc.fc-ayah-07.b: Allah says: We sent it (the clear Book) down during a blessed night; indeed, We were to warn mankind.
fc.fc-ayah-08.f: Quran 2:255 - Ayat al-Kursi: who Allah is
fc.fc-ayah-08.b: No god but Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining; no drowsiness or sleep overtakes Him. All in the heavens and earth is His; none intercedes except by His permission. He knows what is before and after them, and they grasp of His knowledge only what He wills. His Kursi extends over heavens and earth, guarding them tires Him not; He is the Most High, the Most Great.
fc.fc-sunnah-01.f: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell us to eat suhoor?
fc.fc-sunnah-01.b: He said: Take suhoor, for in suhoor there is blessing (Bukhari 1923).
fc.fc-sunnah-02.f: Zayd ibn Thabit ate suhoor with the Prophet ﷺ. How long was it between their suhoor and the adhan?
fc.fc-sunnah-02.b: About the time it takes to recite fifty ayat (Bukhari 1921).
fc.fc-sunnah-03.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about hastening to break the fast?
fc.fc-sunnah-03.b: People will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten to break the fast (Bukhari 1957).
fc.fc-sunnah-04.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ break his fast with?
fc.fc-sunnah-04.b: Fresh dates, before praying. If there were none, dried dates, and if there were none, a few sips of water (Abu Dawud 2356).
fc.fc-sunnah-05.f: What words did the Prophet ﷺ teach a fasting person to say if someone fights or insults them, and how many times?
fc.fc-sunnah-05.b: 'Inni sa'im', meaning 'I am fasting', said twice (Bukhari 1894).
fc.fc-sunnah-06.f: Ibn Abbas compared the Prophet's ﷺ generosity in Ramadan to what?
fc.fc-sunnah-06.b: The free-blowing wind. When Jibreel met him in Ramadan, he was more generous in doing good than the wind sent forth (Bukhari 6).
fc.fc-sunnah-07.f: Until when did the Prophet ﷺ keep up i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan?
fc.fc-sunnah-07.b: Until Allah took his soul. After him, his wives observed i'tikaf too (Bukhari 2026).
fc.fc-sunnah-08.f: When the last ten nights of Ramadan began, whom did the Prophet ﷺ wake up for worship?
fc.fc-sunnah-08.b: His family. Aishah said he would spend the night in worship and wake his family (Bukhari 2024).
fc.fc-sunnah-09.f: How does this hadith end: 'Whoever gives a fasting person something to break the fast with...'?
fc.fc-sunnah-09.b: '...will have a reward like his, without the fasting person's reward being reduced at all' (Tirmidhi 807).
fc.fc-sunnah-10.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about praying the Ramadan night prayer with the imam until he finishes?
fc.fc-sunnah-10.b: Standing in prayer for a whole night is recorded for that person. He said this in Ramadan when the Companions asked him to lead them in prayer for the rest of the night (Tirmidhi 806).
fc.fc-sunnah-11.f: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid al-wisal, joining one day's fast to the next without eating at night?
fc.fc-sunnah-11.b: Out of mercy for his Companions. When they said, 'But you do it', he said: I am not like you; my Lord gives me food and drink (Bukhari 1964).
fc.fc-sunnah-12.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say is the difference between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book?
fc.fc-sunnah-12.b: Eating suhoor, the meal before dawn (Muslim 1096).
fc.fc-sunnah-13.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about a fasting person who forgets and eats or drinks?
fc.fc-sunnah-13.b: He should complete his fast, for it was Allah who fed him and gave him drink (Bukhari 1933).
fc.fc-sunnah-14.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about performing Umrah in Ramadan?
fc.fc-sunnah-14.b: An Umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj (in reward). He told this to an Ansari woman who had missed the Hajj with him (Bukhari 1782).
fc.fc-sunnah-15.f: Bilal used to call the adhan while it was still night. Until when did the Prophet ﷺ say to keep eating and drinking?
fc.fc-sunnah-15.b: Until Ibn Umm Maktum called the adhan, for he did not call it until dawn had broken (Bukhari 1918).
fc.fc-hist-01.f: In Madinah the Prophet ﷺ fasted the day of Ashura and told others to fast it. What changed once fasting Ramadan was prescribed?
fc.fc-hist-01.b: Fasting Ashura became optional: whoever wished fasted it, and whoever wished left it (Bukhari 2002).
fc.fc-hist-02.f: After hearing the ayah about the white thread and the black thread (Quran 2:187), what did Adi ibn Hatim put under his pillow?
fc.fc-hist-02.b: A black cord and a white cord, but he could not tell them apart at night. The Prophet ﷺ explained it means the darkness of night and the whiteness of dawn (Bukhari 1916).
fc.fc-hist-03.f: At Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH), the Prophet ﷺ faced the qiblah and pleaded with Allah, hands stretched out. What did Allah promise?
fc.fc-hist-03.b: To reinforce the believers with a thousand angels, one after another. Umar reports that Quran 8:9 was revealed then (Muslim 1763).
fc.fc-hist-04.f: The Companions who fought at Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH) said their number matched which earlier band of believers?
fc.fc-hist-04.b: The companions of Talut (Saul) who crossed the river with him: just over three hundred and ten men, and only believers crossed with him (Bukhari 3957).
fc.fc-hist-05.f: Why did Uthman ibn Affan miss the Battle of Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH)?
fc.fc-hist-05.b: His wife, a daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, was ill. The Prophet ﷺ told him he would have the reward of a man who was at Badr, and his share of the spoils (Bukhari 3130).
fc.fc-hist-06.f: At the Conquest of Makkah (Ramadan, 8 AH), what did the Prophet ﷺ say as he struck the idols around the Ka'bah?
fc.fc-hist-06.b: 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished' (Quran 17:81). There were 360 idols around the Ka'bah (Bukhari 4287).
fc.fc-hist-07.f: Which surah was the Prophet ﷺ reciting on his she-camel on the day of the Conquest of Makkah?
fc.fc-hist-07.b: Surah al-Fath (The Victory), recited with tarji', a vibrating tone, as Abdullah ibn Mughaffal saw (Bukhari 4281).
fc.fc-hist-08.f: On the day of the Conquest of Makkah, who went inside the Ka'bah with the Prophet ﷺ?
fc.fc-hist-08.b: Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and Uthman ibn Talhah, one of the Ka'bah's key-keepers. The Prophet ﷺ stayed inside a long time and prayed there (Bukhari 2988).
fc.fc-hist-09.f: The Prophet ﷺ was shown that on the morning after Laylatul Qadr he would prostrate in water and mud. How did this come true?
fc.fc-hist-09.b: That night it rained and the mosque's palm-leaf roof leaked. In the morning Abu Sa'id saw traces of water and mud on the Prophet's ﷺ forehead (Bukhari 2027).
fc.fc-hist-10.f: When his wife Safiyyah visited the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque during his i'tikaf, why did he tell two passing men, 'She is Safiyyah'?
fc.fc-hist-10.b: He feared Satan might put a bad thought in their hearts. This was in the last ten days of Ramadan (Bukhari 2035).
fc.fc-qf-01.f: How many surahs are in the Quran, and which one comes last?
fc.fc-qf-01.b: 114 surahs. The last is Surah An-Nas (Mankind), Surah 114.
fc.fc-qf-02.f: Which surah begins the 30th and final juz of the Quran?
fc.fc-qf-02.b: Surah An-Naba (78). Its first word is 'Amma, which is why this juz is known as Juz 'Amma.
fc.fc-qf-03.f: How many ayat does Surah Al-Fatihah have?
fc.fc-qf-03.b: Seven. Al-Fatihah means 'The Opener', and it is the first surah of the Quran.
fc.fc-qf-04.f: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest surah in the Quran?
fc.fc-qf-04.b: Al-Fatihah. He said it is 'the seven oft-repeated (ayat) and the Great Quran' that was given to him.
fc.fc-qf-05.f: Which is the longest surah in the Quran?
fc.fc-qf-05.b: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), Surah 2, with 286 ayat.
fc.fc-qf-06.f: Which is the shortest surah in the Quran?
fc.fc-qf-06.b: Al-Kawthar (Surah 108), with 3 short ayat. Al-Asr and An-Nasr also have 3 ayat, but Al-Kawthar has the fewest words.
fc.fc-qf-07.f: What did the angel first say to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Hira?
fc.fc-qf-07.b: 'Read!' He ﷺ replied, 'I do not know how to read.' This happened three times, then the angel said: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created...' (Al-Alaq 96:1-3).
fc.fc-qf-08.f: Which ayah says that the Quran was revealed in the month of Ramadan?
fc.fc-qf-08.b: Al-Baqarah 2:185. The same ayah says: whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.
fc.fc-qf-09.f: According to Surah 97 of the Quran, on which night was the Quran sent down?
fc.fc-qf-09.b: Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree): 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.' Surah 97 is Surah Al-Qadr.
fc.fc-qf-10.f: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b (Abu al-Mundhir) which ayah in the Book of Allah is the greatest. Which ayah did Ubayy name?
fc.fc-qf-10.b: Ayat al-Kursi (2:255). The Prophet ﷺ praised him: 'May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir!'
fc.fc-qf-11.f: Who told Abu Hurayrah that if he recited Ayat al-Kursi on going to bed, a guardian from Allah would stay with him and no devil would come near him until morning?
fc.fc-qf-11.b: Someone stealing from the Ramadan charity food, who was really a devil (shaytan). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He told you the truth, though he is a liar.'
fc.fc-qf-12.f: Which two ayat did the Prophet ﷺ say will suffice whoever recites them at night?
fc.fc-qf-12.b: The last two ayat of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285-286).
fc.fc-qf-13.f: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say is equal to one third of the Quran?
fc.fc-qf-13.b: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112): 'Say, He is Allah, the One.'
fc.fc-qf-14.f: Which surah of thirty ayat did the Prophet ﷺ say intercedes for a man until he is forgiven?
fc.fc-qf-15.f: Which is the only surah of the Quran that does not begin with 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'?
fc.fc-qf-15.b: Surah At-Tawbah (Surah 9). It opens directly with 'Bara'atun minallahi wa rasulih'.
fc.fc-prep-01.f: Apart from Ramadan, in which month did the Prophet ﷺ fast the most?
fc.fc-prep-01.b: Sha'ban. Aisha (RA) said she never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.
fc.fc-prep-02.f: Did the Prophet ﷺ fast every single day of Sha'ban?
fc.fc-prep-02.b: Aisha (RA) said he fasted Sha'ban except a little, and she never saw him fast a whole month except Ramadan.
fc.fc-prep-03.f: When Usama ibn Zayd noticed how much the Prophet ﷺ fasted in Sha'ban, how did the Prophet ﷺ describe that month?
fc.fc-prep-03.b: 'A month that people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan.'
fc.fc-prep-04.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say happens to our deeds in the month of Sha'ban?
fc.fc-prep-04.b: Deeds are raised up to the Lord of the worlds, and he loved for his deeds to be raised while he was fasting.
fc.fc-prep-05.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about fasting a day or two just before Ramadan?
fc.fc-prep-05.b: None of you should fast a day or two ahead of Ramadan, unless it falls on a fast he regularly keeps.
fc.fc-prep-06.f: In which month did Aisha (RA) make up the Ramadan fasts she owed?
fc.fc-prep-06.b: Sha'ban. She said she could not manage to make them up except in Sha'ban.
fc.fc-prep-07.f: People asked the Prophet ﷺ about the crescent moons. What does the Quran say they are for?
fc.fc-prep-07.b: Allah told him to say: 'They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj (pilgrimage).'
fc.fc-prep-08.f: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Saddidu wa qaribu.' What does it mean?
fc.fc-prep-08.b: Do good deeds properly and in moderation, and if you cannot do them perfectly, come as close as you can.
fc.fc-prep-09.f: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise about how many good deeds to take on?
fc.fc-prep-09.b: Take on the deeds you are able to do, for Allah does not tire (of giving reward) until you tire.
fc.fc-prep-10.f: According to Quran 2:183, why was fasting prescribed for the believers?
fc.fc-prep-10.b: So that you may become righteous (attain taqwa). It was also prescribed for those before us.

prep.intro.title: Ramadan Prep: 30 Days to Get Ready
prep.intro.body: Ramadan is coming, and a beautiful way to welcome it is to arrive ready. Over the next 30 days you will steady your salah, build a daily bond with the Quran, and prepare your body, heart and home, one small step at a time. Go gently, keep going, and make every step for Allah.

prep.day.1.reflect: Which prayer is hardest for me to pray on time, and what usually gets in the way?
prep.day.1.mot: The Prophet ﷺ was asked which deed Allah loves most. He said: prayer offered at its proper time.
prep.p.p1-1.text: Look up today's five prayer times and set an alert a little before each one.
prep.p.p1-1.tip: Use a prayer-times app or your mosque's timetable. An early alert gives you time to finish what you are doing and make wudu.
prep.p.p1-2.text: Pray all five prayers within their times today, ticking each one off as you go.
prep.p.p1-2.tip: Notice which prayer is hardest to catch. That is the one to plan around this week, not a reason to feel bad.
prep.p.p1-3.text: Make a sincere intention that these 30 days are for Allah, and write down why you want to prepare.
prep.p.p1-3.tip: Keep it short and honest, e.g. 'I want to meet Ramadan ready and close to Allah.' Read it again whenever your energy dips.
prep.day.2.theme: Fajr: start the day with Allah
prep.day.2.reflect: How did praying Fajr on time feel, or what would help me catch it tomorrow?
prep.day.2.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever prays Fajr is under the protection of Allah.
prep.p.p2-1.text: Set two alarms for Fajr and put one across the room, so you have to get up to turn it off.
prep.p.p2-1.tip: Make wudu as soon as you are up; the cool water helps you wake. If you oversleep, do not give up: pray it and try again.
prep.p.p2-2.text: Go to bed a little earlier tonight so that waking for Fajr feels easier.
prep.p.p2-2.tip: Count back from Fajr time to find a bedtime that gives you enough sleep, and start winding down half an hour before it.
prep.p.p2-3.text: Ask a family member or friend to be your Fajr partner, checking on each other each morning.
prep.p.p2-3.tip: Agree on a quick message after the adhan. Encouraging each other makes hard mornings far easier to get through.
prep.day.3.reflect: How did taking care over wudu change the way I began my prayers today?
prep.day.3.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever performs wudu and does it well, his sins leave his body, even from beneath his nails.
prep.p.p3-1.text: Make each wudu today slowly and completely, washing every part fully and in order.
prep.p.p3-1.tip: Go slowly but use water sparingly: the Prophet ﷺ made wudu with one mudd, a small amount of water (Bukhari 201).
prep.p.p3-2.text: Learn the dua after wudu and say it each time you finish today.
prep.p.p3-2.tip: Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh (Muslim 234).
prep.p.p3-3.text: Plan how you will make wudu at work, school or when out, so it never makes you late.
prep.p.p3-3.tip: Find the nearest washroom or prayer room in advance. Some people make wudu before leaving home and try to keep it.
prep.day.4.reflect: Which ayah of Al-Fatiha touched me most today, and why?
prep.day.4.mot: Allah said: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant. When he says 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds', Allah says: My servant has praised Me.
prep.p.p4-1.text: Read a simple translation of Al-Fatiha, one ayah at a time, until you know what each line means.
prep.p.p4-1.tip: Write each ayah's meaning on a small card and keep it by your prayer mat. Read it before you pray today.
prep.p.p4-2.text: In at least one prayer today, recite Al-Fatiha slowly, thinking about each ayah as you say it.
prep.p.p4-2.tip: Pause briefly at the end of each ayah. Slowing down a little lets your heart catch up with your tongue.
prep.p.p4-3.text: Reflect on the dua in Al-Fatiha, 'Guide us to the straight path', and the guidance you most need.
prep.p.p4-3.tip: Allah says of Al-Fatiha's last ayat: This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asked (Muslim 395).
prep.day.5.theme: The words of ruku and sujood
prep.day.5.reflect: Which words of my prayer do I now understand that I used to say without thinking?
prep.day.5.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: The nearest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in sujood, so make plenty of dua then.
prep.p.p5-1.text: Learn the meaning of what you say in ruku and sujood, and think of it as you pray today.
prep.p.p5-1.tip: Subhana Rabbiyal 'Adhim: Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great. Subhana Rabbiyal A'la: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
prep.p.p5-2.text: Learn the meaning of the tashahhud (at-tahiyyat) that you recite while sitting.
prep.p.p5-2.tip: Read it line by line with a translation: greetings to Allah, peace on the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous, then the testimony of faith.
prep.p.p5-3.text: Learn the sujood dua 'O Allah, forgive me all my sins' in Arabic, and say it in your sujood today.
prep.p.p5-3.tip: Allahummaghfir li dhanbi kullahu, diqqahu wa jillahu, wa awwalahu wa akhirahu, wa 'alaniyatahu wa sirrahu (Muslim 483).
prep.day.6.reflect: Which Sunnah prayer can I make a lifelong habit, starting this week?
prep.day.6.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever prays twelve voluntary rak'ahs each day for Allah, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.
prep.p.p6-1.text: Pray the two short Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr today, if you do not already.
prep.p.p6-1.tip: The Prophet ﷺ said the two rak'ahs before Fajr are better than this world and all it contains (Muslim 725).
prep.p.p6-2.text: Add one more Sunnah prayer to your day, such as the two rak'ahs after Maghrib.
prep.p.p6-2.tip: Build toward the twelve: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib and 2 after Isha (Tirmidhi 415).
prep.p.p6-3.text: Pray witr before you sleep tonight, so your night ends with prayer.
prep.p.p6-3.tip: The Prophet ﷺ advised Abu Hurayrah to pray witr before sleeping (Bukhari 1981), a good habit if waking at night is hard.
prep.day.7.reflect: Looking back on this week, which salah habit grew most, and which needs more care?
prep.day.7.mot: Successful indeed are the believers: those who are humble and attentive in their prayer.
prep.p.p7-1.text: Pray each prayer today without rushing, letting each position settle before you move on.
prep.p.p7-1.tip: The Prophet ﷺ taught a man who prayed hastily to bow, prostrate and sit until he was at ease in each (Bukhari 757).
prep.p.p7-2.text: Before each prayer today, take a few seconds to silence your phone and clear your mind.
prep.p.p7-2.tip: Face the qiblah, breathe, and remember who you are standing before. A short pause before Allahu Akbar helps focus.
prep.p.p7-3.text: Plan one or two voluntary fasts for the coming week, such as a Monday or Thursday.
prep.p.p7-3.tip: The Prophet ﷺ used to try to fast on Mondays and Thursdays (Tirmidhi 745). Starting gently now makes Ramadan's first days easier.
prep.day.8.reflect: What time of day suits me best for the Quran, and what might get in its way?
prep.day.8.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Read the Quran, for on the Day of Resurrection it will come as an intercessor for its companions.
prep.p.p8-1.text: Choose one fixed daily time for the Quran, such as after Fajr, and read 2 pages in it today.
prep.p.p8-1.tip: Tie it to something you already do, like a prayer. If you cannot read Arabic yet, listen while following a translation.
prep.p.p8-2.text: Put your mushaf or Quran app where you will see it at your chosen time.
prep.p.p8-2.tip: Move distracting apps off your phone's home screen and put the Quran app there. A bookmark saves time finding your page.
prep.p.p8-3.text: Keep praying all five on time, and keep one Sunnah prayer from last week going.
prep.p.p8-3.tip: Tick your prayers off each day so last week's gains are not lost while your focus moves to the Quran.
prep.day.9.reflect: What page goal can I truly keep every day, even on busy days?
prep.day.9.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: The most beloved deed to Allah is the one done regularly, even if it is small.
prep.p.p9-1.text: Write your page goals: about 5 a day by day 14, 10 a day by day 21 and 20 a day by day 29.
prep.p.p9-1.tip: About 20 pages a day completes the Quran in a 30-day Ramadan. If that is too much for now, choose smaller steps you can keep.
prep.p.p9-2.text: Read 3 pages today in your fixed Quran time.
prep.p.p9-2.tip: Each letter you read brings a good deed, multiplied by ten (Tirmidhi 2910). Short daily reading builds the stamina Ramadan needs.
prep.p.p9-3.text: If you have Ramadan fasts to make up, count them today so there is time to fit them in.
prep.p.p9-3.tip: Allah says whoever was ill or travelling makes up an equal number of other days (Quran 2:184). Starting early leaves room.
prep.day.10.reflect: Which recitation mistake will I work on first, and who can help me with it?
prep.day.10.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: The one skilled in the Quran is with the noble, righteous angels, and the one who stumbles over it, finding it hard, has two rewards.
prep.p.p10-1.text: Find a Quran teacher, class or recitation app that can check your reading regularly.
prep.p.p10-1.tip: Ask your mosque about Quran classes, or use an app that listens and corrects. Work on one or two rules at a time.
prep.p.p10-2.text: Listen to a skilled reciter read today's pages before you read them yourself.
prep.p.p10-2.tip: Follow the text with your eyes or finger as you listen, then read it yourself, copying the pronunciation and pace.
prep.p.p10-3.text: Recite the surahs you use in salah to someone who can check your pronunciation.
prep.p.p10-3.tip: Start with Al-Fatiha, the heart of every prayer. Small corrections here improve every prayer you pray.
prep.day.11.reflect: What is Allah telling me in the surah I studied today, and how will I live it?
prep.day.11.mot: A blessed Book which We have revealed to you, so that they may reflect upon its verses and people of understanding may take heed.
prep.p.p11-1.text: Read a simple tafsir of one short surah, such as Al-'Asr or Al-Kawthar.
prep.p.p11-1.tip: Use a trusted tafsir in your language. Read the surah, then its explanation, then the surah again with fresh eyes.
prep.p.p11-2.text: Write down one lesson from that surah and one way you will act on it this week.
prep.p.p11-2.tip: Keep a small Quran journal. One line is enough: what Allah is saying, and one thing you will change because of it.
prep.p.p11-3.text: Recite that surah in one of your prayers today with its meaning in mind.
prep.p.p11-3.tip: Reciting what you understand helps your heart stay present. If you do not know it by heart yet, use a surah you do know.
prep.day.12.reflect: Which ayat do I want to carry in my heart this Ramadan, and why?
prep.day.12.mot: And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?
prep.p.p12-1.text: Memorise one to three new ayat today, repeating each until you can say it without looking.
prep.p.p12-1.tip: Listen to the ayat first, then repeat each one many times before joining them. Revise them after each prayer today.
prep.p.p12-2.text: Recite the ayat you memorised today in one of your prayers.
prep.p.p12-2.tip: Using new ayat in salah helps them stick. If you feel unsure, read them over once more just before you pray.
prep.p.p12-3.text: Teach a child or friend one short surah, or the meaning of one you know.
prep.p.p12-3.tip: The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it (Bukhari 5027).
prep.day.13.reflect: Which surah I once knew has slipped away, and how can I bring it back?
prep.day.13.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Keep revising the Quran, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, it slips away faster than a camel from its rope.
prep.p.p13-1.text: Revise the surahs you already know by reciting them from memory, slowly and carefully.
prep.p.p13-1.tip: Recite to a family member or into a voice note, then check it against the mushaf. Mark any spots that need more work.
prep.p.p13-2.text: Read 5 pages today in your fixed Quran time.
prep.p.p13-2.tip: If this feels like a jump, split it: some pages after Fajr and the rest after another prayer.
prep.p.p13-3.text: Start a small daily charity habit: set aside a coin or a small amount each day until Ramadan.
prep.p.p13-3.tip: Use a jar at home or a donation app. Regular giving, even a little, builds a habit you will carry into Ramadan.
prep.day.14.reflect: Where will the Quran fit in my Ramadan day, and what will I move to make room for it?
prep.day.14.mot: The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Amr: Recite the whole Quran in one month.
prep.p.p14-1.text: Make your Ramadan reading plan: how many pages a day, and at which times.
prep.p.p14-1.tip: One juz a day completes the Quran in 30 days. In the 604-page Madinah mushaf that is about 20 pages, or 4 after each prayer.
prep.p.p14-2.text: Ask a friend or family member to be your Quran partner in Ramadan, to read with or check in with.
prep.p.p14-2.tip: Each night of Ramadan Jibreel met the Prophet ﷺ, who recited the Quran to him (Bukhari 1902). A partner helps on tired days.
prep.p.p14-3.text: Support Quran learning: give to a Quran class or school, or gift someone a translation.
prep.p.p14-3.tip: Ask your mosque or a local Quran school what they need. A mushaf with translation can be a lasting gift for a new reader.
prep.day.15.reflect: What do I hope fasting before Ramadan will teach me about myself?
prep.day.15.mot: Aisha said: I never saw the Prophet ﷺ fast a whole month except Ramadan, nor fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.
prep.p.p15-1.text: Check your fasting plan for late Sha'ban: scholars differ on starting new voluntary fasts after mid-Sha'ban.
prep.p.p15-1.tip: The Prophet ﷺ said not to fast a day or two before Ramadan unless it is a fast you usually keep (Bukhari 1914). Unsure? Ask a local scholar.
prep.p.p15-2.text: On your next fast day, note how your body and mood cope, to guide your Ramadan plans.
prep.p.p15-2.tip: Jot down energy dips, hunger times or headaches. These notes will shape your suhoor, iftar and sleep plans this week.
prep.p.p15-3.text: Read 6 pages today in your fixed Quran time.
prep.p.p15-3.tip: If you are fasting, the quiet hour before iftar is a lovely time to read and make dua.
prep.day.16.reflect: What helps me keep commitments to Allah that no one else sees?
prep.day.16.mot: Aisha said: I would have Ramadan fasts to make up, and I could only make them up in Sha'ban.
prep.p.p16-1.text: If you owe any fasts, book a date for each one before Ramadan and put them in your calendar.
prep.p.p16-1.tip: Spread them out if that is easier. If you are unsure what you owe or how to make it up, ask a trusted local scholar.
prep.p.p16-2.text: Support anyone at home who is making up fasts: wake them for suhoor or help prepare their iftar.
prep.p.p16-2.tip: Many people have days to make up. Ask what would help, then do it quietly and kindly.
prep.p.p16-3.text: After each of the five prayers today, say SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar 33 times each.
prep.p.p16-3.tip: Complete 100 with 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir' (Muslim 597).
prep.day.17.reflect: What keeps me up late, and what am I willing to let go of to sleep earlier?
prep.day.17.mot: The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Amr: Pray at night and also sleep, for your body has a right over you.
prep.p.p17-1.text: Choose a regular bedtime that gives you enough sleep before Fajr, and start it tonight.
prep.p.p17-1.tip: The Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before Isha and chatting after it (Bukhari 568). Count back from Fajr to set your bedtime.
prep.p.p17-2.text: Try the Sunnah bedtime routine tonight: wudu, lie on your right side and say the bedtime dua.
prep.p.p17-2.tip: The Prophet ﷺ taught al-Bara this routine with a dua beginning 'Allahumma aslamtu wajhi ilayk' (Bukhari 6311).
prep.p.p17-3.text: Pray Isha on time tonight, then keep the rest of the evening calm so you can sleep early.
prep.p.p17-3.tip: Dim the lights, put screens away and lay out what you need for the morning. A calm evening makes Fajr easier.
prep.day.18.reflect: What would a calm, unhurried suhoor look like in my home?
prep.day.18.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Eat suhoor, for there is blessing in suhoor.
prep.p.p18-1.text: Plan three or four simple suhoor meals you can rotate through Ramadan.
prep.p.p18-1.tip: Choose foods that keep you going, such as oats, eggs, yoghurt, dates and fruit, with plenty of water. Prep the night before.
prep.p.p18-2.text: On your next fast day, wake early enough to eat suhoor calmly before Fajr.
prep.p.p18-2.tip: Eating close to Fajr follows the Sunnah: the gap between the Prophet's suhoor and the adhan was about fifty ayat (Bukhari 1921).
prep.p.p18-3.text: Read 8 pages today in your fixed Quran time.
prep.p.p18-3.tip: Try reading part of it in the quiet time after suhoor or Fajr, when the house is still and the mind is fresh.
prep.day.19.reflect: How can my iftar table become a place of gratitude and sharing, not just eating?
prep.day.19.mot: The Prophet ﷺ would break his fast before praying with fresh dates; if there were none, dried dates; and if none, a few sips of water.
prep.p.p19-1.text: Plan iftars that begin simply with dates and water, followed later by a moderate meal.
prep.p.p19-1.tip: Keep dates and water ready before sunset so you can break your fast on time. Batch-cook a few meals ahead to save time.
prep.p.p19-2.text: Plan how you will pray Maghrib on time after breaking your fast, at home or at the mosque.
prep.p.p19-2.tip: Break the fast lightly, pray, then sit down to eat. Agree this routine with your household so no one feels rushed.
prep.p.p19-3.text: Choose a night in Ramadan to share iftar with a neighbour, a relative or your local mosque.
prep.p.p19-3.tip: Whoever gives a fasting person food to break their fast gets the same reward, without reducing theirs (Tirmidhi 807).
prep.day.20.reflect: Which food or drink habit has a hold on me, and how will I loosen it before Ramadan?
prep.day.20.mot: O children of Adam... eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.
prep.p.p20-1.text: If you drink tea or coffee, have one cup less today and keep easing off until Ramadan.
prep.p.p20-1.tip: Swap that cup for water or a caffeine-free drink. Cutting down slowly now can make the first days of fasting easier.
prep.p.p20-2.text: Swap one sugary snack or drink today for fruit, dates, nuts or water.
prep.p.p20-2.tip: Notice when you reach for sugar out of habit or boredom, and keep a better option in your bag or kitchen.
prep.p.p20-3.text: Read 9 pages today, using an old coffee or snack break for some of them.
prep.p.p20-3.tip: Replacing a habit with a better one is easier than just stopping. Keep your mushaf or Quran app near your usual break spot.
prep.day.21.reflect: What do I want fasting to change in me this Ramadan, beyond going without food?
prep.day.21.mot: O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may become righteous.
prep.p.p21-1.text: Draft your Ramadan daily timetable from suhoor to sleep, built around the fast and the five prayers.
prep.p.p21-1.tip: Block out suhoor, prayers, Quran, work or school, a rest, iftar and night prayer. Leave some gaps; a realistic plan lasts.
prep.p.p21-2.text: Decide where you will pray the night prayers of Ramadan, and check your mosque's timings.
prep.p.p21-2.tip: If you will pray at home, set up a space and choose what you will recite. A plan made now is easier to keep.
prep.p.p21-3.text: Read 10 pages today: try 2 pages after each of the five prayers.
prep.p.p21-3.tip: That is half a Ramadan day's reading. Notice how it fits around your prayers; next week you will build on it.
prep.day.22.reflect: How does Allah's promise of mercy change the way I see my mistakes, and what will I change?
prep.day.22.mot: Say: O My servants who have wronged themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
prep.p.p22-1.text: Sit alone for a few minutes, think of the sins you want to leave, and sincerely ask Allah to forgive you.
prep.p.p22-1.tip: Tawbah means stopping the sin, regretting it, resolving not to return, and putting right any wrong done to others.
prep.p.p22-2.text: Choose one habit you want to leave before Ramadan and take one step away from it today.
prep.p.p22-2.tip: Remove the trigger: delete the app, avoid the place, or tell a trusted friend. Put something good in its place.
prep.p.p22-3.text: Pray two rak'ahs today, then sincerely ask Allah for forgiveness.
prep.p.p22-3.tip: Whoever sins, then makes wudu well, prays two rak'ahs and asks Allah's forgiveness, Allah forgives him (Abu Dawud 1521).
prep.day.23.reflect: Why do I really want this Ramadan to be different, and who am I doing it for?
prep.day.23.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah records one full good deed; if he does it, ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times or more.
prep.p.p23-1.text: Write three intentions for Ramadan, for Allah's sake: one for worship, one for character, one for others.
prep.p.p23-1.tip: Be specific, e.g. 'pray Fajr on time', 'control my anger', 'call my aunt weekly'. Keep the list where you will see it daily.
prep.p.p23-2.text: Before each good deed today, pause and renew your intention to do it for Allah alone.
prep.p.p23-2.tip: A quick inner reminder is enough: 'This is for You, O Allah.' Work, study and cooking can be done with that intention too.
prep.p.p23-3.text: Read 12 pages today, renewing your intention before you open the mushaf.
prep.p.p23-3.tip: Read to be guided, not only to finish. Pause at one ayah that speaks to you and note it down.
prep.day.24.reflect: If I could ask Allah for only three things this Ramadan, what would they be?
prep.day.24.mot: When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me.
prep.p.p24-1.text: Start your Ramadan dua list: what you want to ask Allah for, for yourself and for others.
prep.p.p24-1.tip: Include this life and the next, family, friends, the sick and the wider Ummah. Keep it on your phone so it is always with you.
prep.p.p24-2.text: Make dua from your list after one of your prayers today, asking with full hope.
prep.p.p24-2.tip: Add duas from the Quran and Sunnah too. The Prophet's most frequent dua was 'Allahumma rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah...' (Bukhari 6389).
prep.p.p24-3.text: Ask a family member or friend what they would like you to pray for, and add it to your list.
prep.p.p24-3.tip: When you pray for a fellow Muslim in their absence, the angel appointed to you says: 'Amin, and for you the same' (Muslim 2732).
prep.day.25.reflect: Whose relationship with me needs mending, and what small step can I take this week?
prep.day.25.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: The one who truly keeps family ties is not the one who returns kindness, but the one who reconnects when ties are cut.
prep.p.p25-1.text: Reach out to one relative or friend you have drifted from, with a kind message or a call.
prep.p.p25-1.tip: Keep it simple: a salam, a dua or asking after their health. You do not need to fix everything at once; just open the door.
prep.p.p25-2.text: Apologise to someone you have wronged, or quietly forgive someone who wronged you.
prep.p.p25-2.tip: If a relationship is not safe, you can keep a healthy distance and still make dua for them. Forgiveness starts in the heart.
prep.p.p25-3.text: Read 15 pages today; if time is short, listen to some of them while travelling or cooking.
prep.p.p25-3.tip: Listening keeps you connected on busy days. Follow along in the mushaf when you can, so your eyes learn the pages too.
prep.day.26.reflect: How can I make giving a joyful daily habit rather than a once-a-year duty?
prep.day.26.mot: The Prophet ﷺ made zakat al-fitr a purification for the fasting person from idle and indecent talk, and food for the poor.
prep.p.p26-1.text: Set your Ramadan charity budget and choose the causes you will support.
prep.p.p26-1.tip: Split it across the month so you give something every day. Think of local needs, relatives in need and trusted charities.
prep.p.p26-2.text: Find out your mosque's zakat al-fitr amount and deadline, and note it for each person you pay it for.
prep.p.p26-2.tip: The Prophet ﷺ made it due on every Muslim, young or old, and ordered it paid before the Eid prayer (Bukhari 1503).
prep.p.p26-3.text: Check this week's prayers and fix the one that most often slips past its time.
prep.p.p26-3.tip: Look at what got in the way and make one small change, like an earlier alarm or a reminder before you leave work.
prep.day.27.reflect: What do I want my family to remember about this Ramadan in years to come?
prep.day.27.mot: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it.
prep.p.p27-1.text: Hold a short family or household meeting to share Ramadan goals and share out the chores.
prep.p.p27-1.tip: Let everyone, even young children, choose one goal. Shared chores mean everyone gets time to pray, read and rest.
prep.p.p27-2.text: Agree on one prayer each day in Ramadan that your household will pray together.
prep.p.p27-2.tip: Maghrib after iftar or Isha before bed often suits families. Let children take turns choosing a dua to say afterwards.
prep.p.p27-3.text: Set up a family charity jar that everyone, including the children, adds to during Ramadan.
prep.p.p27-3.tip: Agree together where it will go, and let the children help hand it over so they see the good it does.
prep.day.28.reflect: What would I need to change in my routine to give the last ten nights my very best?
prep.day.28.mot: Aisha said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ strove in worship in the last ten nights more than at any other time.
prep.p.p28-1.text: Plan your night prayers for the last ten nights: where you will pray, when and for how long.
prep.p.p28-1.tip: Lighten those days if you can: book time off, cook ahead and agree family routines, so the nights get your best.
prep.p.p28-2.text: Choose a few duas to repeat in the last ten nights, and add them to your dua list.
prep.p.p28-2.tip: In the last third of every night Allah says: Who is calling on Me, that I may answer him? (Bukhari 1145).
prep.p.p28-3.text: Mark the last ten nights in your calendar, highlighting the odd ones, as nights to give your best.
prep.p.p28-3.tip: The Prophet ﷺ said to seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten (Bukhari 2017). Confirm the dates once Ramadan begins.
prep.day.29.reflect: How many hours did screens take from me last week, and what could those hours become in Ramadan?
prep.day.29.mot: The Prophet ﷺ said: There are two blessings that many people lose out on: good health and free time.
prep.p.p29-1.text: Check your screen-time report and set a daily limit for Ramadan.
prep.p.p29-1.tip: Most phones show daily use in settings. Set app limits, mute busy group chats and turn off notifications you do not need.
prep.p.p29-2.text: Choose screen-free times for Ramadan, such as suhoor, the hour before iftar and the night prayers.
prep.p.p29-2.tip: Charge your phone outside the bedroom and use a simple alarm clock. Let friends know you will reply less in Ramadan.
prep.p.p29-3.text: Read 20 pages today as a test run: 4 pages after each of the five prayers.
prep.p.p29-3.tip: If you do not finish, note how far you got. That is your honest starting point, and you can build from there.
prep.day.30.reflect: Looking back on these 30 days, what has changed in me, and what will I carry into Ramadan?
prep.day.30.mot: The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Quran was revealed as guidance for people... Allah intends ease for you, not hardship.
prep.p.p30-1.text: Choose the one salah habit you will guard most closely in Ramadan, and write it down.
prep.p.p30-1.tip: Look back at week one: on time, Fajr, wudu, meaning, Sunnah prayers and focus. Pick one and ask Allah to help you with it.
prep.p.p30-2.text: Set out your mushaf, bookmark and page plan so you can start reading on the first day.
prep.p.p30-2.tip: Keep the mushaf where you pray and write your daily target on your bookmark. Begin on day one, even if just a few pages.
prep.p.p30-3.text: Read your intentions and dua list again, and ask Allah to help you make the most of Ramadan.
prep.p.p30-3.tip: Check your suhoor food, iftar plan, bedtime, charity plan and screen limits too. Then rest: you have prepared well.
prep.ms.1.title: Salah foundations
prep.ms.1.goal: Pray all five on time, guard Fajr, make wudu with care, understand what you recite and add the Sunnah prayers.
prep.ms.2.title: Quran connection
prep.ms.2.goal: Keep a fixed daily Quran time, grow to about 5 pages a day, check your recitation and understand a short surah.
prep.ms.3.title: Fasting and body
prep.ms.3.goal: Follow the Sunnah in your fasts, book any make-up days, reset your sleep, plan suhoor and iftar, and ease off caffeine and sugar.
prep.ms.4.title: Heart and community
prep.ms.4.goal: Turn to Allah, set intentions, write a dua list, mend ties, plan charity and the last ten nights, and build up to about 20 pages a day.
guide.today.title: Today and the daily checklist
guide.today.body: Today shows your progress for the current day of Ramadan, your next prayer or iftar time, the hadith of the day and the checklist of deeds in seven groups: salah and dhikr, Quran, character, charity, the last ten nights (from day 21), things to avoid, and the Abu Bakr challenge. Tick a deed when you have done it. Turn on detail mode to see each deed's source, a short explanation and its authenticity grade.
guide.points.title: Points and progress
guide.points.body: Each deed is worth a few points, shown next to it. Your daily percentage is the share of today's deeds you ticked. Points earned on days 21 to 30 count one and a half times, because the Prophet ﷺ strove hardest in the last ten nights (Muslim 1175).
guide.quran.title: Quran tracker
guide.quran.body: Log the pages you read after each session. The standard Madani mushaf has 604 pages in 30 juz, so about 20 pages a day completes it in Ramadan. The tracker shows your juz, the pace you need for the days left, and a chart of your reading.
guide.learn.title: Learn: quiz and flashcards
guide.learn.body: Learn turns the hadith and verses behind every deed into true-or-false cards, multiple-choice questions and flashcard decks (Ramadan words, duas, verses about fasting, Sunnahs of fasting, Ramadan in history, Quran facts and preparing for Ramadan). Flashcards use spaced repetition: cards you know come back less often, cards you miss come back sooner. Today's 5 is a short daily mix that builds a learning streak. Every answer shows its source.
guide.prep.title: Ramadan Prep
guide.prep.body: A 30-day programme to get ready before Ramadan begins. It starts with a short self-check, then gives three small actions each day: first fixing your salah (praying on time, Fajr, the Sunnah prayers, understanding what you recite), then building a daily connection with the Quran, then fasting practice and habits, and finally the heart, family and charity. Daily salah and Quran check-ins show your readiness. During Sha'ban the plan follows the Hijri date, so it ends as Ramadan begins; you can also start it at any time from the Me tab.
guide.compete.title: Competitions
guide.compete.body: Schools, universities, mosques, companies, families and communities can run a Ramadan competition. An organiser creates one with up to ten prizes and shares the six-letter join code, a QR poster or personal invitation links. Participants join with the code and a display name; their points, days logged and Quran pages update a live leaderboard for individuals and for classes or teams. Only a display name and totals are shared, never which deeds you ticked. Organisers can set a daily points cap, review flagged entries, export results and print certificates for everyone at Eid.
guide.prayer.title: Prayer times and iftar
guide.prayer.body: Allow your location (or enter coordinates) to see today's prayer times and a countdown to iftar and to the end of suhoor. Choose the calculation method your community follows in settings. Your location stays on your device unless you turn on reminders.
guide.streaks.title: Streaks
guide.streaks.body: Four streaks count consecutive days on which you ticked Fajr, Isha, any Quran deed (recitation, reflection or listening) and charity (giving charity or feeding a fasting person). The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small (Bukhari 6464).
guide.badges.title: The 12 badges
guide.badges.body: First Step: tick anything on day 1. Week One: log something on each of days 1 to 7. Halfway: log something on each of days 1 to 15. Fajr Warrior: a 7-day Fajr streak. Tahajjud Master: Tahajjud on 7 nights. Quran Lover: recitation or reflection on 15 days. Generous: charity on 10 days. Abu Bakr: all four Abu Bakr deeds in one day. Abu Bakr Gold: that on 3 different days. Last 10 Hero: at least 5 of the last ten days logged with an average of 70% or more. Perfectionist: 100% on 3 days. Champion: 60% or more on 20 days.
guide.last10.title: The last ten nights
guide.last10.body: In the Islamic calendar each night comes before its day, so the 21st night begins at sunset on day 20. From that evening the app marks the odd nights (21, 23, 25, 27 and 29) on the evenings they begin, and from day 21 the checklist adds a section for the last ten days and nights. The Prophet ﷺ told us to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten (Bukhari 2017), so make the most of each of them.
guide.sisters.title: Sisters' mode
guide.sisters.body: Turn this on during your period. Prayer and fasting deeds are set aside and left out of your percentage, so your score reflects the worship that applies to you: dhikr, dua, listening to the Quran, charity, service and character.
guide.modes.title: Modes and the Hijri date
guide.modes.body: The app follows the Hijri calendar (Umm al-Qura). In Ramadan it sets the day automatically, in Sha'ban it suggests Ramadan Prep, and the rest of the year it tracks Sunnah fasts (Mondays, Thursdays and the 13th to 15th of each month), the six days of Shawwal and the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah. If your community sighted the moon a day earlier or later, adjust it by one day in settings. You can also choose the mode yourself.
guide.journal.title: Reflection journal and Eid report
guide.journal.body: Write a line each day about what you learned or want to improve. On Eid, download a PDF report with your days, Quran pages, streaks, badges and reflections — a keepsake, and a way to celebrate children's effort.
guide.account.title: Account and sync
guide.account.body: Everything works without an account and stays on your device. Create one if you want a backup and to sync between phone, tablet and computer. You can delete the account and its cloud data at any time.
guide.languages.title: Languages
guide.languages.body: The app is available in English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian and Urdu, with right-to-left layout for Arabic and Urdu. Translations of hadith and verse meanings are for understanding; follow the source link for the authoritative text.
guide.privacy.title: Privacy and your data
guide.privacy.body: Your tracker data lives on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you join a competition (display name and totals), create an account (for sync), turn on reminders, share your progress, or use the explain feature. Export a backup file or reset everything from the data section.
